title: Founding Design Engineer | CodeSpeak
descriptionHtml:
Role: Founding Design Engineer (Senior / Staff)

Company: CodeSpeak

Location: London, on-site. Ideally you already live in London. Candidates based elsewhere are welcome to apply, and remote is possible for a very strong candidate, but UK-based candidates come first. Candidates with a Global Talent visa, granted or in process, are a good fit.

Job Type: Full-time

About CodeSpeak

Agents write more code every month. Human brains stay the same. CodeSpeak is building a program model that sits one level above code, so people can see how a program works and changes over time without reading much of it. The goal is to give control back to the developer: you think about architecture, and the routine goes away.

CodeSpeak was founded by Andrey Breslav, the creator of Kotlin, which millions of developers use daily. Around him is a team that has built the tools other engineers rely on, at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph, and Elastic. When it comes to program analysis and developer tooling, these are some of the best people in the world. CodeSpeak is backed by Accel and by funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, and funding covers several years.

Here is the open problem. The team has a fair idea of what the program model should look like. It does not yet know how to visualise it. As Founding Design Engineer you will decide how it looks, then build it and ship it. The core engineering team has just been hired, and nobody on it has design-engineering skills. You are the missing piece.

CodeSpeak is a UK company. It has no business in Russia and no ties to Russian companies. It is still testing which problems it can solve best, so priorities may shift.

What you are expected to do:

Design and delivery

  • Own how people interact with CodeSpeak: in the CLI, on the web and on any future platform.

  • Design the interfaces yourself. Build many prototypes, decide on the right UX and ship the result.

  • Harden the prototypes users liked, so they hold up on real data, with the same care for performance and product quality as for design.

  • Ship features to production without help from the rest of the team.

Product problems

CodeSpeak works with unusually complex information: developer intent, requirements, code, architecture, the relationships between them, how they change over time, contradictions and dependencies. The job is not to display it, but to help developers understand it, navigate it and act on it.

  • Find a way to visualise CodeSpeak's new, higher-level program model.

  • In your first 30 days, visualise the architecture of a codebase split into components. Go deeper from there: a single component, its diff and its code review.

  • Then interfaces that let developers navigate structured requirements and how they relate to each other, review requirements alongside code review, see how requirements map onto parts of the codebase, explore how intent, architecture and code change over time, browse agent sessions, find contradictions between requirements, and edit and reorganise requirements rather than only view them.

  • Web UI is the simplest and most obvious platform. Some of this will live in the console. VS Code plugins and other desktop frameworks may follow, and the final scope is still open.

Ways of working

  • Find tasks and clarify requirements without waiting for a brief. Nobody will micromanage you. Egor and Andrey give general direction.

  • Work directly with the founder and the engineering team to turn early ideas and hypotheses into intuitive, interactive product experiences.

  • Take part in design meetings, where many decisions are made on the spot.

  • Explain and defend your design decisions to Egor and Andrey. Both hold strong opinions, and both argue hard.

  • Argue for your tasks, and step back with good grace if the team disagrees.

What you need to succeed:

Craft

  • You can design an interface, prototype it and ship it to production on your own.

  • You have strong design taste, and your portfolio shows it: UX, interaction design, information architecture and visual hierarchy. For this role the portfolio is critical.

  • You make complex information or a complex data model easy to read. Think maps with metadata or dense dashboards, with non-trivial state. Tools that read and write count for more than infographics or landing pages.

  • You have solid computer science and software engineering fundamentals, plus TypeScript, and deep experience building production apps with modern UI frameworks such as React. At least 3 years of delivering production software.

  • You understand the problems of engineers, because engineers are CodeSpeak's users.

How you work

  • You can say why you made each design choice. "I'm an artist, I see it this way" will not work here.

  • You are curious and self-directed, and you care about making programming better. You gather requirements and find projects yourself.

  • You actively improve your own workflow with AI-powered coding tools.

  • You work hard and can be reached when a task needs it. The team has no weekend-work culture.

  • You think fast and explain your reasoning clearly.

  • You speak Russian, which is the team's working language. This is a priority, not a hard rule, and a strong candidate without Russian will still be considered.

Nice to have

  • A background as a frontend engineer with good taste. Engineers from SwiftUI, desktop, mobile or full-stack are welcome if they visualise complex things very well.

  • Experience with complex data visualisation.

  • Some sense of what an early-stage startup is like. A big-tech engineer who knows what they are joining can fit, and so can a former co-founder.

A technical degree is not required. Self-taught people and people with degrees in geology or biology have done well in roles like this.

What you get:

  • An unsolved problem with real room for your taste. The team is inventing a new way to represent programs, and you decide how it looks.

  • A boutique team of strong engineers, built carefully, who have built developer tools at Google, Databricks, Perplexity, JetBrains, Sourcegraph and Elastic.

  • An ML team of four, led by Emeli Dral. She co-founded Evidently, an evals startup, and co-authored a very popular Coursera course for data scientists.

  • Day-to-day work with Egor, Andrey and the tech lead.

  • Backing from Accel and from funds that also invested in Hugging Face and Mistral, with funding for several years.

  • A UK contract with a pension and medical insurance.

  • Autonomy. You set your own tasks and nobody hovers over you.

  • Work in AI, a field most people want to be in.

title: Founding Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The Role

This is Dust's first PM hire. You'll work closely with the product team, turning raw GTM signal, company priorities, and user feedback into well-formed problems the team can act on.

What you will change:

  • A lot of product signal doesn't reach the team in an actionable shape today. You'll create and run the process that connects signal to shaping to prioritization.

  • Implementing company strategies across functions requires ownership and orchestration. You'll translate company priorities into an intelligible, trackable set of product, marketing, and operations initiatives.

  • You'll enrich prioritized projects with distilled business and user context and market perspective so that the people building them make better decisions.

Our designers and engineers stay close to product decisions from conception to delivery. You're here to make their context richer and their priorities sharper. You enable distributed ownership, you don't replace it.

What You'll Do

  • Qualify and synthesize feedback: Sit at the intersection of GTM, users, and product. Turn high-volume, unstructured input into a small set of well-framed problems worth solving.

  • Shape initiatives: Work with engineers and designers to translate validated problems into initiatives ready for Stack Rank — with clear objectives, KPIs, and scope.

  • Drive outcome tracking: Own reporting on whether what shipped actually moved the needle. Feed that back into the next round of decisions.

  • Improve internal coordination: Connect Marketing, Comms, GTM, and Product — reduce the friction that slows things down when multiple functions need to move together.

  • Own outcomes, not outputs: For cross-functional initiatives, you'll own the goal — objectives, KPIs, orchestration, reporting.

  • Own artefacts in the Dust platform (agents, skills, data, etc..) to continuously rewire and augment the above for yourself and the team

What You Can Expect

Team

Dust is a growing team of about a 100 people. Most of the product and engineering team is based in Paris, with close collaboration across our teams in New York, San Francisco, and London.

The interview process

The process is designed to understand how you think, collaborate, and operate in an ambiguous, technical environment:

  • Recruiter conversation: motivation, background, logistics, and fit for an early-stage environment.

  • Hiring DRI conversation: discussion with a senior member of the product team.

  • Product exercise: collaboration exercise based on a real company priority.

  • Founder conversation: discussion with one of our founders on product judgment, attitude, and ability to operate with distributed authority.

  • Onsite: working sessions with members of Engineering, Design, and GTM. We’ll look at how you gather context, identify the important problems, collaborate on possible approaches, and leave ownership with the people closest to the work.

We care more about the quality of your reasoning and collaboration than about arriving at a predetermined answer.

What We're Looking For

  • Founding PM mentality: Senior individual contributor and builder balancing capacity to build the practice in the company while being hands-on.

  • 5–8+ years of product experience, including time at an early-stage company where you had to build process from scratch.

  • Genuine product taste. You know great from good in the world of tech products, and you bring deep perspective, judgment and conviction to any preferences you voice.

  • Excellent information synthesis skills, distilling a messy pile of customer feedback, sales calls, and Slack threads into sharp problems.

  • Technical proficiency earn the respect of engineers. You don't need to code, but you understand systems and tradeoffs easily deeply.

  • Builder mindset at heart. You use AI tools fluently and you're excited about what they unlock for how PMs operate. You've thrived in environments where everyone is a builder and you want to strengthen that.

  • Effective communication. You'd rather say one clear thing than three vague things.

  • Comfort with distributed authority. You influence by being right, not by being in charge.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.

title: Full-Stack Engineer - Ads Engine
descriptionHtml:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role
We build an ads engine that learns as it goes: brand book, taste, and what actually performs in every market. It plans, generates, localizes, launches and learns from ads across the major ad platforms, using ElevenLabs’ full audio and video stack.
You’ll be a founding engineer for a product area of your own. There’s no PM and no handed-down spec. You’ll talk to users, decide what to build, and ship it across the stack, from data pipelines and agent tools to the UI. Early work could include feeding competitive intelligence into the engine’s weekly briefs or launching a new ad format.
We’re looking for founders and founding engineers. You’d rather ship a rough v0 on Friday than a perfect design doc. Strong engineering is the minimum. What sets people apart is product judgment and ownership.

Requirements

  • Has built and shipped a product end-to-end without anyone handing them a spec, ideally as a founder or one of the first engineers.

  • Strong full-stack product engineer (frontend- or backend-leaning is fine) who can build a pipeline, an agent tool and the UI

  • Builds with LLMs and agents pragmatically: tools, retrieval and evals, not model research.

  • Talks to users without being asked, and can say what they’d build first and why.

Bonus: experience with ad platforms, adtech or marketing tools; analytics and attribution; web builders and CMSs; taste in creative.

Location
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere between the US East Coast and India, with the ability to operate in European timezones required. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in Bangalore, Dublin, London, New York and Warsaw.

#LI-Remote

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

title: Genesis-World: Core Simulation Engine Engineer
descriptionHtml:
What we’re building

Robots will learn in simulation before they hit the factory. Genesis-World is our bet on that future.

Genesis-World is an open-source, general-purpose simulation platform for physical AI from Genesis AI. One unified multi-physics engine: rigid bodies, FEM, MPM, particles, cloth, fluids. A robot arm can pour water onto sand, grasp a deformable object, or cut a soft body, all in the same simulation. Nyx, our in-house renderer, may be the most promising renderer for robotics out there: real-time photo-realistic rendering, advanced features like depth of field, and state-of-the-art techniques never seen before. Sensors of every kind: cameras, lidar, IMU, contact forces, temperature, plus arguably the most advanced tactile simulation available (paper). And the engine keeps growing: we are developing internally the most comprehensive and fastest Incremental Potential Contact (paper) solver for deformable body dynamics we know of, soon to be open-sourced. It powers real business applications, from full-fledged box packaging with labelling machine and all, to wire harnessing and lab automation, without any physics hack or compromise.

Everything is Python-first and runs anywhere. Kernels are written once, and Quadrants, our in-house JIT compiler, lowers them to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86, and ARM64. A single laptop or a datacenter. Massively batched GPU simulation for learning at scale, and complex non-batched scenes where CPU wins outright.

This is at the core of Genesis AI’s strategy. Evaluation is the bottleneck of scalable robotics: real hardware caps iteration at wall-clock time, but simulation turns it into a compute problem. Ours already runs two orders of magnitude faster than hardware (tens of thousands of episodes in half an hour instead of 200+ hours), while correlating with on-hardware rollouts at 89%. The north star: physical AI that improves at the speed of compute.

The role

Simulation is still a hard sell in robotics. Outside a few success stories, like reinforcement learning for locomotion, most teams skip it, and friction is a big part of why: painful to use, painful to debug. We live that pain ourselves: debugging a failing experiment during policy evaluation takes 30 minutes, and there is no way to automatically generate a standalone reproduction script. That blocks adoption, even internally.

Your job is to kill that friction. You build the software engineering backbone of Genesis-World: everything that makes a large, fast-moving simulation codebase reliable, maintainable, frictionless. And it all ships in the open. Every hour of pain you remove, you remove for every roboticist who comes after you.

You join as core maintainer of Genesis-World, with shared stewardship of the whole platform from day one. Our physics team develops the algorithms, but just as importantly, you work to make everything around them excellent: infrastructure, tooling, APIs, architecture.

The problems waiting for you

  • Make testing of a JIT-compiled engine scalable. Running our full suite is already taking hours because the ratio between compile time and runtime can be as bad as x10. Getting rid of this bottleneck is a serious challenge that will require a joint effort from the Genesis-World and the compiler teams.

  • Make any bug reproducible. Dump and reload simulations bit-exactly, across machines, across backends, even when a single timestep of a batched simulation can already max out VRAM. Turn any failing run into a standalone reproduction script, automatically.

  • Make autodiff first-class. Genesis-World is differentiable today, but partially: memory-hungry, slower than it could be, and hard to maintain due to manual operation recording. The project spans the engine and the compiler: you drive the requirements on Quadrants and iterate in a tight loop with the compiler team until the integration is solid.

  • Edit scenes at frozen time. See the scene, move entities and robots around, iterate on layout, all without building the scene or compiling the engine. Authoring today means a full build cycle. Make it instant.

  • Make the simulator extensible. First-class plugins for physics solvers and interactive viewer backends, including Nyx. Sensors already work this way. Generalize it, and Genesis-World becomes a platform others build on.

  • Give robots real actuation. Motors and MIMO transmissions, cleanly abstracted at the interface between users and the physics engine.

  • Make time a local variable. Today the clock and the timestep are global to the engine, which forbids whole classes of speedups: environments cannot step independently, the timestep cannot adapt to the state, and individual solvers cannot advance at their own rate. Free the clock down to the sub-scene level and let the simulation fly.

  • Make scenes come alive. Events triggered by physics: press the button and the microwave door pops open, squeeze the trigger and the drill spins.

  • Keep the core sharp. Refactoring legacy subsystems, stronger typing, consistent coding style, less Python overhead on hot paths, full scene serialization, telemetry and replay.

Beyond the code: you review issues and pull requests with the core team, answer questions from users and contributors, and can join the push on adoption.

Who you are

You care about the engineer using what you build as much as the thing itself. A slow test, a cryptic error, a manual step: you see it, you go after the root cause, and you remove it for everyone. You have opinions about API design.

You are comfortable with physics and robotics: the right design choices take a working picture of what a simulator like Genesis-World does, how it works, and how it is used, a picture you can partly build on the job.

  • Strong Python engineering on large codebases: architecture, refactoring, typing, packaging, performance profiling (py-spy, Nsight, Xcode Instruments, RenderDoc).

  • Developer tooling, test infrastructure, or CI at scale.

  • Enough fluency with JIT compilation, code generation, or GPU computing stacks to reason about compilation caching, kernel dispatch, and startup cost. You will work closely with Quadrants.

  • At ease debugging across the full platform matrix: Windows, Linux, and macOS, on x86 and arm64, over CUDA, AMD, and Apple Metal (and possibly Intel XPU via Vulkan soon)

  • Open-source reflexes: triaging issues, reviewing external pull requests, communicating with a community.

Bonus points: experience with other robotics simulators (Drake, MuJoCo, Newton, Isaac, RaiSim, Jiminy, Brax). PyTorch, our user-facing interface. Other JIT compilers such as Triton, JAX, or Numba. 3D tooling and interactive editors (Maya, Blender, Houdini). Serialization formats (USD, glTF, MJCF/URDF). C++, CUDA, or Metal. Developer relations or community work.

title: GRC Security Specialist
descriptionHtml:
About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

The role

We are formalising our security assurance function. We have technical controls and the engineering culture; what we need now is the governance layer that proves it - to our auditors, to our funders, and to our regulator.

You will be the delivery engine behind that. You will own the recurring assurance cycle end to end, run our third-party security programme, and be the person who turns evidence into something a due diligence team or a certification auditor can be satisfied by.

You will be responsible for building controls, gathering evidence, and challenging suppliers.

What you will own:

1. Third-party security assurance

- Run security due diligence on new suppliers, maintain initial questionnaire to risk sign-off, working with Procurement and Legal on security and data protection schedules.

- Maintain a supplier tiering model based on criticality and run the periodic re-assessment cycle for tiered suppliers: certification expiry, subprocessor changes, breach notifications, SLA performance.

- Maintain the supplier and outsourcing registers, including preparation for the FCA's material third party register under PS26/2 (rules in force 18 March 2027).

- Track concentration risk and exit plans for critical suppliers.

2. Inbound due diligence and customer assurance

- Own our response to security due diligence from funders, banking partners, institutional investors, commercial partners and prospects.

- Build and maintain a reusable trust pack: answer library, security whitepaper, current certifications, pen test attestations, standard questionnaire pre-fills (SIG, CAIQ).

- Turn a 40-hour bespoke questionnaire response into a 4-hour one.

3. The assurance calendar

- Maintain the annual calendar of security activities and make sure each one happens, produces evidence, and closes its actions: penetration tests, access reviews, disaster recovery tests, tabletop exercises, policy reviews, supplier re-assessments, awareness training.

- Coordinate external penetration tests: scoping, vendor selection, scheduling, findings triage, remediation tracking, retest.

- Facilitate tabletop exercises, including scenario design and post-exercise action tracking.

4. Risk and control administration

- Maintain the information security risk register: run the assessment cycle, record treatment plans with named owners and dates, chase closure.

- Administer the policy exception and risk acceptance process, ensuring every exception is owned, time-bound and reviewed on expiry.

- Perform first-line control testing: sample-test where key controls operate as designed and retain the evidence.

- Produce security MI for the Head of Security to take to ExCo and the Risk Committee.

5. Vulnerability and findings management

- Consolidate findings across sources — EDR, cloud security posture, SAST/DAST/SCA, secrets scanning, penetration tests — into a single view with agreed severity definitions and remediation SLAs.

- Triage, route and chase remediation with engineering teams; escalate ageing findings.

- Own the reporting on remediation performance.

6. Security awareness

- Run the awareness programme: induction, annual refresher, phishing simulation, role-based training for engineers, completion tracking.

- Coordinate pre-employment screening with People.

What you will contribute to:

- The ISO 27001 ISMS, which we are building towards certification. You will draft and maintain control documentation, populate the Statement of Applicability, gather evidence, coordinate the internal audit programme and be a primary point of contact for our external auditor. The Head of Security owns the framework, scope, and risk appetite.

- Policies and standards: you will draft, review and shepherd policies through approval, and track the review cycle.

- Incident response: you will maintain the IR plan and playbooks, facilitate post-incident reviews, track remediation actions, and support regulatory notification (ICO personal data breach reporting within 72 hours; FCA notification under Principle 11 / SUP 15.3).

- Business continuity and DR: you will maintain the documentation and the testing evidence.

- Secure development: you will help embed security requirements into the SDLC and support threat modelling sessions.

- Data protection: you will support RoPA maintenance, DPIA completion and DSAR handling alongside Legal.

What success looks like:

First 90 days: you know our supplier estate and have tiered it; the assurance calendar for the next 12 months is published and owned; inbound due diligence requests come to you and go out without the Head of Security rewriting them.

Six months: the trust pack exists and is being used; the risk register is live with owned treatment plans; ISO 27001 evidence collection is systematic rather than a scramble; the exception register exists.

Twelve months: supplier re-assessment runs on a cadence without prompting; the material third party register is ready ahead of the March 2027 deadline; MI to the Risk Committee is trusted.

Essential experience:

- Three or more years in an information security assurance, GRC or security compliance role, at least some of it in a regulated financial services environment or another environment with real external audit pressure.

- Hands-on experience of ISO 27001, whether operating an ISMS or taking one through certification.

- Demonstrable experience running third-party or vendor security assessments, and of responding to inbound security due diligence.

- Comfortable reading technical findings — an EDR vulnerability report, a penetration test finding, a cloud misconfiguration — and forming your own view on severity and real-world exploitability rather than passing the vendor's rating through unchanged.

- Clear, concise written English. Much of this role is writing things that external parties will judge us on.

- The confidence to chase a busy engineer, challenge a supplier's assertion, and tell us when an answer is not good enough.

Desirable:

- Experience of a cloud-native environment, ideally AWS.

- Experience of scaling a control framework as an organisation grows.

- Familiarity with UK operational resilience expectations (SYSC 15A) and outsourcing requirements (SYSC 8).

- Certifications such as CISM, CISA, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, CRISC or CCSP. We care more about what you have done than what you hold.

What we offer

  • Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity

  • Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days per year

  • One month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership through WellHub

  • Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

title: Group Agency Director
descriptionHtml:
Overview

Captify, now part of Verve Group, is the leading Search Intelligence Platform for the open web and the largest independent holder of first-party search data outside of Google, connecting the real-time searches from over 2 billion devices globally. Its Search Intelligence technology powers omnichannel programmatic advertising and real-time insights for the world’s biggest brands, such as Disney, Unilever, eBay, Mercedes-Benz, Microsoft, Nestlé, GSK, Uber, Mars, P&G, Sony and Toyota—without reliance on third-party cookies. Captify brings brands more customers, publishers greater yield and consumers the most relevant digital experiences.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and passionate Sales Planner to work alongside the Sales team to create growth opportunities with new and existing clients. You will be responsible for identifying key marketing opportunities, delivering best in class audience insights and supporting the commercial teams with your client and vertical expertise. In this role you will play a crucial part in helping drive commercial success and growth for the business.

What we're looking for

As Group Agency Director, you will own Captify's relationship with Publicis Groupe and be accountable for growing revenue across the group. You will lead a team of agency-facing sellers, set the strategy for the patch, and make Captify a go-to partner for Publicis agencies and their clients.

This is a senior commercial role. It combines hands-on relationship building at leadership level with team management, forecasting and close work with our product, data and operations teams.

  • Reports to: VP of Sales 
  • Location: London, hybrid
  • Direct reports: 3/4

What you'll do 

Revenue growth

  • Own and deliver the annual revenue target for the Publicis Groupe patch, including new and repeat business.
  • Build a clear account plan across Publicis agencies and networks, identifying where Captify can grow share of spend.
  • Lead pitches, proposals and upfront or partnership negotiations at agency and holding-group level.
  • Keep an accurate pipeline and forecast, and report performance to the leadership team.

Relationship leadership

  • Be the senior point of contact for Publicis Groupe, building trusted relationships from trading and investment leads through to agency and client leadership.
  • Position Captify's search intelligence as a strategic asset for planning, activation and insight, not only a media line.
  • Spot opportunities to work directly with key Publicis clients alongside their agencies.
  • Stay close to the group's priorities, structure changes and trading arrangements.

Team management

  • Lead, coach and develop a team of agency-facing sellers.
  • Set clear targets, run regular pipeline and performance reviews, and support the team on key deals.

Working across Captify

  • Work with Client Success, Product, Insights and Trading to deliver campaigns that perform and grow.
  • Feed agency and client needs back into product and commercial strategy.
  • Share wins, case studies and best practice with the wider commercial team.

What you'll bring

  • Significant experience in agency-facing sales or partnerships in ad tech, data or digital media, with a strong track record of hitting and beating revenue targets.
  • Established senior relationships within Publicis Groupe (for example Publicis Media, Starcom, Zenith, Spark Foundry, Digitas or Epsilon) and a good understanding of how the group plans and trades.
  • Experience leading and developing a commercial team, ideally including people managers or senior sellers.
  • Confidence negotiating at holding-group level, including partnership and investment deals.
  • A solid grasp of programmatic, audience data, measurement and the privacy-led changes shaping digital advertising.
  • A consultative, insight-led selling style, and the ability to turn data into a clear commercial story.
  • Strong forecasting and pipeline discipline, plus comfort with CRM tools such as Salesforce.
  • Energy, resilience and a collaborative approach to working across teams.

What success looks like in 12 months

  • Revenue from Publicis Groupe is growing in line with or ahead of target.
  • Captify is active across more Publicis agencies and clients, with a clear plan for the next year.
  • A partnership or preferred-supplier agreement is in place or in active negotiation at group level.
  • The team is fully staffed, hitting its targets, and has clear development plans.
  • Pipeline and forecasting are accurate and trusted by leadership.

What We Offer

  • Boost your professional knowledge with our annual training budget & internal webinars

title: Growth Lead / Acquisition Lead
descriptionHtml:
FORREST is a new purpose-driven brand dedicated to walking, creation, and finding balance between nature and culture.

An independent label born in France, FORREST designs and crafts premium walking bags in its own workshop, alongside its artisans, with a deep commitment to quality, sustainability and responsible production.

At the crossroads of fashion, urban culture and outdoor design, FORREST wants to offer more than products: a new relationship to walking, creativity, slowness and the physical world.

We are preparing our e-commerce launch and are looking for a senior Growth Lead to help us structure our digital acquisition strategy without compromising the brand’s cultural and premium positioning.

Tasks

As Growth Lead / Acquisition Lead, you will be responsible for building and piloting the first acquisition system for FORREST.

Your role will be to turn our brand universe into a clear, measurable and scalable acquisition strategy.

You will work directly with the founders and help us define what to test, where to invest, how to measure performance, and how to grow without damaging the brand.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Build a 90-day digital acquisition plan for the launch.
  • Define the right channel mix: Meta Ads, Google Search, Google Shopping, Performance Max, retargeting, CRM, newsletter, content and collaborations.
  • Structure the acquisition funnel from traffic to conversion.
  • Identify and test the most relevant creative angles for FORREST.
  • Work with creative teams to brief and evaluate performance assets.
  • Coordinate media buying, CRM, tracking and creative specialists when needed.
  • Set up a simple but useful reporting system.
  • Analyse CAC, ROAS, conversion rate, average order value, cost per lead, email sign-ups and margin impact.
  • Recommend budget allocation and scaling decisions.
  • Help improve the e-commerce journey: landing pages, product pages, reassurance, storytelling, checkout and post-purchase flows.
  • Translate learnings into clear weekly decisions.

The mission is not only about buying traffic. It is about building a learning system that helps us understand our audience, our strongest messages and our best acquisition channels.

Requirements

We are looking for a senior profile with strong experience in digital acquisition for DTC, e-commerce or premium consumer brands.

You should have experience with:

  • Launching or scaling DTC brands.
  • Physical products and e-commerce.
  • Premium or high-consideration purchases.
  • Paid acquisition, especially Meta and Google.
  • CRM, email flows and lead generation.
  • Shopify or similar e-commerce environments.
  • Funnel analysis and conversion optimisation.
  • Creative testing and performance storytelling.
  • Working directly with founders or small senior teams.

You are not just a media buyer. You are able to connect brand, business, creativity and data.

You should be comfortable discussing:

  • CAC
  • ROAS
  • margins
  • conversion rate
  • creative angles
  • brand positioning
  • customer journey
  • acquisition budget
  • testing methodology

We are looking for someone pragmatic, structured and senior enough to challenge us when needed.

Freelance / fractional role. Initial mission: 3 months. Possible extension after the launch phase. Expected rhythm: 1.5 to 2 days per week. Remote possible. Regular working sessions with the founders. Start: as soon as possible.

title: Head of Compliance (12 month FTC)
descriptionHtml:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better.

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 300 territories globally.

The Role:

As Compliance & Risk Lead, you are a key member of Paddle’s compliance team, reporting to our VP, Compliance. You work closely with legal, product, and operational teams to ensure Paddle remains compliant with global payments and fintech regulations as we scale rapidly.

The Paddle compliance function is critical to our operations and growth, enabling innovation while maintaining trust with customers and regulators. You lead the compliance team and collaborate across teams, bringing expertise in payments compliance, risk management, and reporting. You are instrumental in building robust systems to track, analyze, and report on compliance, ensuring Paddle stays ahead in a dynamic regulatory landscape.

The role is based in the UK but global in scope, reflecting Paddle’s international reach.

What you'll do:

You will partner with our Compliance, legal and other teams across Paddle to integrate compliance into our operations, with a heightened focus on building scalable monitoring and reporting:

  • Team leadership: Hire, onboard, and manage compliance professionals, fostering a collaborative and high-performing team to support Paddle’s global compliance needs.

  • Payments compliance: Develop and refine compliance policies and procedures to ensure adherence to global card scheme rules, consumer protection laws and payments regulation (as applicable).

  • Compliance monitoring: Design and oversee simple tech-enabled monitoring programs to track compliance with internal policies and external regulations, using data-driven tools to identify trends and potential risks proactively.

  • Reporting: Deliver compliance reporting for internal stakeholders at all levels (e.g. senior leadership, the Board, product teams) and external regulators, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and clarity to demonstrate Paddle’s regulatory adherence.

  • Risk management: Develop and manage Paddle’s enterprise risk management program, collaborating with teams across the business to identify risks, embed controls and report on their effectiveness.

  • Regulatory research: Work with the legal team to stay ahead of evolving payments, consumer and fintech regulations, advising on their impact and integrating findings into monitoring and reporting frameworks.

  • Incident response: Lead investigations into high-risk complaints and/or compliance breaches, coordinating with legal and operational teams to resolve issues, and produce detailed incident reports for internal review and regulatory submission as needed.

We'd love to hear from you:

  • You have 6-8 years of compliance experience, ideally in payments and/or in fast-growing businesses, with a proven ability to implement and manage scalable monitoring and reporting systems.

title: Head of Data (London)
descriptionHtml:
Own Conveo's data, from the warehouse to the dashboard, and build the team every part of the business relies on.

This role can be based from either our London or Antwerp location.

Conveo is building the AI-powered infrastructure for consumer understanding, making consumer and B2B research fast, affordable and high quality. Global brands such as Unilever, Google and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across their marketing, product and research teams.

Backed by Y Combinator, we're in a period of rapid growth. We started this year with around 20 people and are on track to reach around 120 by year end, so the people who join now have an outsized chance to shape how the company is built.

We raised a $50M Series A led by DST Global, giving us the fuel to move even faster. We’re investing in our product, growing an exceptional team, and taking on bigger challenges as we enter our next stage of growth.

The Role

You'll be our first Head of Data. You'll own internal data at Conveo and build the team that serves the whole company with it.

You won't be starting from a blank page. Our GTM engineering team has built a data warehouse and semantic layer and has made a start on BI, and colleagues in operations have helped shape our metric definitions. What we don't have is one person who owns all of it, knows what good looks like, and turns it into something every team trusts and uses.

You'll report to our CFO and work very closely with our CTO, as well as with the engineering team, operations and go-to-market. This is a hands-on role. You'll be in the data yourself, not writing a strategy and handing it over. You'll start as the first member of the data team, with a remit to hire as we grow.

This is a role for the long term, not an audit-and-leave project. It starts with the foundations and grows into a bigger team, with room for machine learning and data science to help us predict more across the business.

What You'll Do

Own the data stack end to end

  • Take ownership of our warehouse (Google BigQuery), our transformation and semantic layers (dbt and Cube today) and our BI tooling (Metabase today)

  • Review what's been built with a critical eye, and get it ready to scale as new tools and data sources come in

  • Think through access rights, so it's clear who can see customer, HR and financial data once it all lives in one place

Build one source of truth the business trusts

  • Own metric definitions, so every team works from the same numbers

  • Close the gaps that matter most, starting with areas like marketing attribution and the data our finance team needs for its analysis

  • Make our data reliable enough that people trust it and act on it

Turn data into insight for every team

  • Sit down with department leads, get to the real question behind a request, and build the analysis that answers it

  • Act as the translator between engineering and the business: ask engineers the hard questions about what to build, and explain data in plain English to everyone else

  • Swap today's sprawl of one-off dashboards and AI-generated reports for a clear set of things people actually need to look at

Use AI well, without the slop

  • Shape our data so AI tools can use it reliably

  • Help the business get real value from AI for analysis, without a flood of low-quality output

Build the data team

  • Hire your first team members, and set out what the BI team should look like as we grow

  • Lay the groundwork for machine learning and data science later on

What Success Looks Like

  • After one month: you know our data infrastructure properly and have run a full gap analysis covering what we take in, what we understand and what's missing. You also have a plan for what to fix first and a plan for the team, including your first hires.

  • After three months: you've reviewed the setup in place and own BigQuery, the transformation layer and our BI tooling, and our systems are ready to scale. Teams are already using data better because of work you've delivered.

  • After six months: every department is running with deep insights and analytics, and our leaders have the confidence and ability to use the data themselves.

  • Throughout: people trust the numbers, the business has the dashboards it needs rather than a thousand it doesn't, and we know who the data team hires next.

What You'll Bring

  • Experience leading data at a startup or scale-up, as a Head of Data, Head of Analytics or similar. Ideally you've been at a Series B company or later and have seen what good structure looks like at the next stage

  • Hands-on BI and analytics experience. You've done the insights work, not only data engineering, and you know what good BI looks like

  • Enough technical depth to ask engineers the hard questions, and a clear understanding of how data flows from the warehouse through transformation and semantic layers into a BI tool.

  • A problem solver's instinct: you can talk to a department lead, draw out what they really need, and turn it into analysis

  • A commercial mindset: you understand how a business works and what it needs from its data

  • Strong stakeholder skills. Lots of people will want your time, and you prioritise well while keeping their trust

  • Everyday use of AI in how you work, and a view on how to build data that AI tools can rely on

  • Experience of the challenges that come with scaling fast, and a clear sense of the structure you'll bring as we grow

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with BigQuery, dbt, Cube or Metabase

Why join us?

  • Work directly with frontier AI models and push what they can actually do.

  • Join a YC-backed team that's growing fast and gives you room to grow with it.

  • Competitive salary (£115k-£130k) and meaningful equity. We want you to own a real piece of what we're building.

  • Offices in London, Antwerp, and New York. We work best together, so we ask for 3 days a week in the office.

  • Regular socials: rooftop drinks, team dinners, run clubs, and more.

  • Twice-yearly off-sites to places worth travelling to. Austria, Las Vegas, and Portugal.

  • Private health coverage with Vitality (incl. dental, vision)

  • Enhanced employer pension contribution (5% employer, 3% employee contribution)

  • Refer someone great and earn up to £5,000.

title: Head of Data Science
descriptionHtml:
What do we do?

Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better. 

We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally. 

The role:  

We are looking for a Head of Data Science to build Paddle's data science capability from the ground up. Our Merchant of Record model gives us a data position no PSP or billing provider has: subscription and pricing context alongside granular payment-outcome data, across thousands of software businesses. This role exists to turn that into economic value by putting machine learning and agentic systems into production.

The mandate is deliberately narrow and deliberately ambitious: data science at Paddle owns automated decisioning inside the product — traditional machine learning and agentic systems alike — not decision-support analytics.

We have a long list of candidate opportunities than we can fund, spanning payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance. We have a working hypothesis about which of these pays back first, and we'll share it — but part of the job in your first quarter is to pressure-test it, size the alternatives yourself, and tell us where to start.

This is a founding role, and for the first few quarters it is a building role more than a managing one. You'll be the only person in the function: doing the analysis, engineering the features, training and evaluating the models or agents, taking the first system live with our engineering teams — and then operating it, answerable for its uptime, its drift and its numbers. Once the first use cases are proving out, you'll hire and lead a hub-and-spoke team of data scientists and machine learning engineers embedded across our highest-value business areas. You'll report into the VP of Data and work in close partnership with Product, Payments, Engineering, Risk and Finance.

What you'll do: 

  • Prioritise which opportunities have the biggest impact.. Build a value-based use-case backlog across payment performance and revenue recovery, sales and marketing operations, growth and monetisation intelligence, and risk, trust and compliance; size the leading candidates properly; and make the call on sequencing with the relevant Product, Risk, RevOps and Finance stakeholders. This gets refreshed quarterly.

  • Personally deliver the first system end to end: the analysis and back-test, the features, the model, policy or agent, the deployment, and the shadow and A/B tests that prove it works. Not a spec handed to someone else to build.

  • Operate what you deploy. Own monitoring, retraining, drift response, incident handling and rollback for live decisioning, alongside the engineering teams whose services call it — and set the expectation that the function runs its systems rather than shipping them.

  • Work across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and be honest about which a problem actually needs: a propensity or uplift model, a policy of rules, or an agent with tools, evals against golden answer sets and trace-level observability. Several of our strongest candidate use cases point each way.

  • Build and lead the team — hire senior data scientists embedded in value areas and machine learning engineers in the hub, and set the professional standards, shared methods and reusable components the function runs on.

  • Establish the production stack alongside Data Platform and Engineering: reproducible training data, code and artefacts; a model registry; inference services with real latency, availability and rollback requirements; historically accurate features where decisions need backdated reconstruction; eval harnesses and trace observability for agentic workflows; and monitoring for data quality, drift, model performance and economic outcomes. Start ad hoc where that's sufficient and platformise once the first use cases have shown what's actually needed.

  • Own value capture end to end. Shadow-test and A/B test every deployment against the incumbent strategy, translate metric movement into a financial number on a methodology co-signed by Finance, and publish a quarterly report on realised value.

  • Set the governance model for automated decisioning — proportionate risk assessment, clear ownership, latency and availability requirements, human escalation and rollback — working with Legal, Privacy, Compliance and Risk on GDPR, EU AI Act and payments obligations, and producing the evidence early enough to shape the design.

  • Define the boundaries and the working relationship with Product Science, Analytics Engineering, Data Platform and AI Enablement, so accountability for decision support versus automated decisioning stays unambiguous.

  • Deliver cross-functionally: embed in delivery groups with product owners, domain experts and platform engineers rather than handing models over the wall.

We'd love to hear from you if you:

  • Experienced leading data science or ML teams that own systems in production, with deployments that moved a commercial metric and kept running afterwards. Proofs of concept and dashboards are not what we're hiring for.

  • Hands-on now, not formerly. Your first quarters are spent writing SQL and Python, engineering features, evaluating models and agents, and doing the work that gets a system live — not reviewing someone else's.

  • Experienced across both traditional ML and agentic systems, and clear about how they differ in practice: propensity and uplift models, feature pipelines and drift on one side; tool and context design, prompt and retrieval iteration, evals against golden answer sets and trace observability on the other.

  • Practised at running live systems rather than just launching them — monitoring, retraining, incident response, rollback, and the on-call reality of a decision the business depends on.

  • Pragmatic about method: happy to argue for rules or heuristics where they capture most of the value, and to reserve models and agents for where they genuinely earn their keep.

  • Comfortable with an undefined starting point. There's a long list of candidate use cases and a strong internal hypothesis, but no fixed roadmap — you'll be expected to form your own view, back it with numbers, and defend it to an executive audience.

  • Strong on measurement — experimentation, uplift modelling, back-testing — and willing to hold your own work to a financial number that Finance will scrutinise.

  • Fluent in the engineering side of production ML and agents (training pipelines, model registries, inference services, feature stores, drift detection, trace observability) and able to hold your own with senior engineers on latency, availability, observability and rollback.

  • Able to hire, level and develop senior data scientists and ML engineers, and to set standards for a function that doesn't exist yet.

  • Credible with executives and commercial stakeholders: you can take a use case from business problem to value estimate to prioritisation decision, and say no to low-value work.

  • Experienced in payments, fintech, subscriptions, high-volume commercial operations or another regulated transactional domain — enough to get to a credible value estimate in a new area quickly.

  • Comfortable treating regulated ML as a design constraint rather than paperwork — model risk assessment, DPIAs, auditability, traceability of model and policy versions to production decision logic.

Everyone is welcome at Paddle

At Paddle, we’re committed to removing invisible barriers, both for our customers and within our own teams. We’re committed to building a diverse team where everyone feels safe to be their authentic self. Let’s grow together.

 

Why you’ll love working at Paddle

We’re a diverse, growing group of Paddlers who pride ourselves on our transparent, collaborative and respectful culture.

We live and breathe our values, which are:

  • Paddle Together - “None of us, is as smart as all of us”

Connecting at Paddle

We’re a ‘digital-first’ company, which means our Paddlers always have the freedom to choose where, when and how they work within our hub locations.

title: Head of Operations (m/w/d) | Health & Beauty Scale-up
descriptionHtml:
MY HEALTH & BEAUTY ist Deutschlands erstes Health&Beauty-Startup mit dem Ziel, hochwertige ästhetische Medizin und Longevity-Health Behandlungen für eine breite Zielgruppe zugänglich, unkompliziert, bezahlbar und flächendeckend verfügbar zu machen.

Innerhalb von nur drei Jahren sind wir auf 10 Standorte und mehr als 50.000 Kunden gewachsen. Damit gehören wir zu den am schnellsten wachsenden Unternehmen im Bereich der ästhetischen Medizin in Deutschland.

Und wir stehen erst am Anfang.

In den kommenden Jahren wollen wir unseren Wachstumskurs deutlich beschleunigen und MY HEALTH&BEAUTY als die führende Marke für ästhetische Medizin und Longevity etablieren.

Unser Erfolgsmodell basiert auf einem klaren Anspruch: höchste medizinische Qualität ohne Kompromisse zugänglich für Alle.

Unsere Behandlungen werden ausschließlich von Ärzten durchgeführt. Wir arbeiten mit den hochwertigsten Produkten führender Hersteller und setzen auf standardisierte Prozesse, intensive Schulungen und eine konsequent hohe Behandlungs- und Servicequalität.

Unser Ziel ist nicht der kurzfristige "Verkauf" einzelner Behandlungen, sondern der Aufbau langfristiger Kundenbeziehungen durch Qualität, Vertrauen und ein konstant exzellentes Kundenerlebnis.

Der Markt für ästhetische Medizin und Longevity wächst sehr stark. Gleichzeitig verändern sich die Erwartungen der Kunden: Behandlungen sollen professioneller, zugänglicher und selbstverständlicher werden.

Genau diese Entwicklung treiben wir mit MY HEALTH & BEAUTY aktiv voran.

Aufgaben

Für die nächste Phase unseres Wachstums suchen wir einen Head of Operations, der die operative Entwicklung unserer HEALTH&BEAUTY Lounges verantwortet und gemeinsam mit uns die Grundlage für die nächsten 10, 20 oder 100 Standorte schafft.

Wir suchen ausdrücklich keinen Verwalter bestehender Strukturen.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Strukturen hinterfragt, Schwachstellen erkennt, Lösungen entwickelt und diese konsequent umsetzt.

Jemanden, der strategisch denkt und selbst vor Ort ist, mit Teams arbeitet, Trainings durchführt, Probleme löst und Verantwortung übernimmt.

Deine Verantwortung

Du trägst die operative Gesamtverantwortung für unsere Standorte und entwickelst gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung unsere Operations kontinuierlich weiter.

Leadership & People

Du führst unsere Kollegen und späteren Führungskräfte und sorgst dafür, dass Führung nicht nur auf dem Papier stattfindet, sondern im täglichen Geschäft spürbar ist.

Du entwickelst Mitarbeiter weiter, gibst klares Feedback und schaffst Verantwortlichkeiten.

Du erkennst Leistungsträger frühzeitig, entwickelst sie weiter.

Genauso konsequent gehst du mit Underperformance um.

Du sorgst gemeinsam mit unserem Recruiting Team dafür, dass unsere Standorte jederzeit mit den richtigen Menschen besetzt sind und wir auch bei starkem Wachstum oder Ausfällen unsere personellen Standards halten.

Training & Development

Du entwickelst strukturierte Trainings- und Weiterbildungsprogramme für unsere operativen Teams.

Du führst Trainings selbst durch und entwickelst gleichzeitig Strukturen, mit denen Wissen innerhalb der Organisation skalierbar weitergegeben werden kann.

Du etablierst klare Standards für Onboarding, Führung, Verkauf, Kundenservice und operative Abläufe.

Dabei misst du nicht nur, ob Trainings stattgefunden haben, sondern ob sie tatsächlich zu besserer Performance führen.

Operational Excellence

Du analysierst die operativen Prozesse des Unternehmens und stellst sie kontinuierlich infrage.

Was funktioniert, wird standardisiert.

Was nicht funktioniert, wird verändert.

Was unnötig kompliziert ist, wird vereinfacht.

Du entwickelst SOPs, Verantwortlichkeiten und Prozesse, die für jeden Standort klar verständlich und reproduzierbar sind.

Dein Anspruch ist, dass ein Kunde unabhängig vom Standort ein konstant hohes MY-HEALTH-&-BEAUTY-Erlebnis erhält.

Performance & KPIs

Du definierst gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung die relevanten operativen KPIs und stellst sicher, dass diese verstanden und konsequent gesteuert werden.

Dazu gehören insbesondere Produktivität, Personaleinsatz, Auslastung, Umsatzperformance, Kundenbindung, Servicequalität und operative Effizienz.

Wenn ein Standort seine Ziele verfehlt, analysierst du nicht nur die Zahlen, sondern findest heraus, warum.

Anschließend entwickelst du konkrete Maßnahmen, definierst Verantwortlichkeiten und stellst deren Umsetzung sicher.

Customer Experience & Qualitätsanspruch

Wir wollen nicht durchschnittlich gut sein.

Unser Anspruch ist ein außergewöhnlich hohes Niveau in jedem einzelnen Standort.

Du stellst sicher, dass unsere Standards hinsichtlich Kundenservice, Organisation, Sauberkeit, Auftreten, Kommunikation und operativer Qualität konsequent eingehalten werden.

Du erkennst Abweichungen frühzeitig und greifst ein, bevor aus kleinen Problemen strukturelle Probleme werden.

Dein Ziel ist klar:

Aus 10 erfolgreichen Standorten eine skalierbare, professionelle Operations-Struktur zu bauen, die auch mit weiteren 20, 30 oder 100 Standorten funktioniert.

Qualifikation

Diese Position ist bewusst nicht für jeden geeignet.

Wir suchen einen außergewöhnlich leistungsorientierten Menschen mit einem sehr hohen eigenen Anspruch.

Du solltest bereits bewiesen haben, dass du Menschen führen, operative Strukturen verbessern und Verantwortung für Ergebnisse übernehmen kannst.

Was du zwingend mitbringen solltest

Mehrjährige relevante Führungserfahrung in einer anspruchsvollen operativen Organisation.

Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Führung größerer Teams und mehrerer Führungsebenen.

Idealerweise hast du bereits Verantwortung für mehrere Standorte oder dezentrale operative Einheiten getragen.

Du hast Erfahrung darin, Mitarbeiter nicht nur zu verwalten, sondern tatsächlich zu entwickeln, zu motivieren und leistungsfähiger zu machen.

Du kannst professionelle Trainingskonzepte entwickeln und bist gleichzeitig stark genug in Kommunikation und Auftreten, diese Trainings selbst durchzuführen.

Du bist zahlengetrieben und kannst aus KPIs konkrete operative Entscheidungen ableiten.

Du hast bereits Prozesse aufgebaut oder grundlegend verbessert und kannst konkrete Beispiele nennen, bei denen deine Arbeit messbar zu besseren Ergebnissen geführt hat.

Du kannst gleichzeitig strategisch und extrem hands-on arbeiten.

Du kommunizierst klar, direkt und verbindlich und scheust dich nicht davor, auch unangenehme Entscheidungen zu treffen.

Du besitzt ein ausgeprägtes Verantwortungsgefühl und wartest bei Problemen nicht darauf, dass dir jemand sagt, was zu tun ist.

Was uns besonders wichtig ist

Wir suchen keine Person, die möglichst viele Aufgaben delegiert und Operations hauptsächlich aus Meetings und Reports heraus steuert.

Wir suchen jemanden, der das Unternehmen wirklich verstehen will.

Jemanden, der regelmäßig in unseren Standorten präsent ist.

Der mit Mitarbeitern spricht.

Der Kunden beobachtet.

Der Prozesse selbst durchläuft.

Der Probleme sieht, bevor sie in einem Dashboard auftauchen.

Und der anschließend Strukturen schafft, damit diese Probleme dauerhaft gelöst werden.

Du solltest einen außergewöhnlich hohen Anspruch an Qualität, Geschwindigkeit und Umsetzung haben.

Wir arbeiten in einem stark wachsenden Unternehmen. Damit gehen Veränderung, hohe Geschwindigkeit und Phasen außergewöhnlicher Belastung einher.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Verantwortung nicht an seiner Stellenbeschreibung oder an der Uhr festmacht. Wenn eine wichtige Standorteröffnung ansteht, ein Team Unterstützung benötigt oder ein operatives Problem gelöst werden muss, erwarten wir Ownership und die Bereitschaft, die Extrameile zu gehen.

Was für uns zählt, sind Ergebnisse.

Dein Mindset

Du denkst unternehmerisch.

Du willst gestalten statt verwalten.

Du stellst hohe Anforderungen an dich selbst und an dein Team.

Du kannst Menschen begeistern, aber genauso klare Grenzen setzen.

Du bist extrem lösungsorientiert.

Du suchst bei Problemen nicht nach Erklärungen, warum etwas nicht funktioniert, sondern nach dem schnellsten nachhaltigen Weg, es zu lösen.

Du kannst Prioritäten setzen und auch unter erheblichem Druck klar entscheiden.

Du hast keine Angst vor Verantwortung.

Benefits

Was wir dir bieten

Eine Schlüsselposition mit direktem Einfluss auf die weitere Entwicklung und Skalierung von MY HEALTH&BEAUTY.

Überdurchschnittliche Vergütung mit attraktivem Fixgehalt und leistungsabhängigem Bonus.

Firmenwagen, auch zur privaten Nutzung.

Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung und kurze Entscheidungswege.

Die Möglichkeit, Strukturen nicht nur zu übernehmen, sondern ein Operations-System für die nächsten 20, 30 oder 100 Standorte aktiv mit aufzubauen.

Keine Konzernbürokratie und keine endlosen Abstimmungsschleifen. Gute Ideen können schnell entschieden und umgesetzt werden.

Und vor allem: eine Rolle, in der du wirklich etwas aufbauen kannst, anstatt lediglich einen bestehenden Betrieb zu verwalten.

Du möchtest nicht einfach einen weiteren Job. Du möchtest maßgeblich daran beteiligt sein, ein Unternehmen von 10 Standorten zu der führenden Marken seiner Branche zu skalieren.

Wenn du dich darin wiederfindest und bereits nachweislich auf einem hohen Niveau gearbeitet hast, möchten wir dich gerne kennenlernen.

title: Head of Operations (Zürich, 100%)
descriptionHtml:
We are hiring a Head of Operations


⏰ Start date: ASAP

📍Zürich, Switzerland (on-site, remote not possible)

🦾 Full-time (100%)

Loki Robotics’ mission is to make physical services an abundant commodity for everyone through robotics and physical AI. We build, deploy and operate expert robots with unique capabilities to automate commercial facility services at scale. We believe emergent capabilities in physical AI are unlocked by taking a straight shot to useful, performant robots deployed in the real world. We’re a tight team that takes initiative, operates with agency, and genuinely cares about doing outstanding work.

Your role

Every robot we produce has to be prepared, shipped, deployed, operated, serviced and improved in the field. As Head of Operations, you own that end to end. You are the execution engine that customers and the rest of Loki rely on to make deployments happen, and you build the operations organization that keeps getting better at it: more automated, more productized and spread across more roles and geographies as we scale.

What you will be doing

  • Own deployment implementation: site assessments, customer kick-offs, onsite supervision, staff training, performance assessment and all customer communication along the way

  • Run logistics for every deployment: fulfillment, shipping, import/export, compliance and coordination with the customer’s receiving side

  • Build and run the operations organization: SOPs, scheduling, allocating operator bandwidth across deployments, testing and internal data collection, among others

  • Work with our testing engineers on release, performance and quality assurance testing: reporting procedures, schedules and the bandwidth to execute them

  • Relay what customers and field operations tell you back to product, GTM and R&D

  • Find operations bottlenecks and remove them, whether through a new process, a new hire, a change in structure or by killing a process entirely. Many ops tasks exist because a feature is missing or because that is how it has always been done. Your job is to delete, automate or productize them

  • Hire, onboard and lead the operations team: define roles, onboarding, incentives, internal assessments and the KPIs that steer our operations organization

  • Train partner operators and distributors in deployment operations as we expand

What you should have

  • 5+ years in operations, field deployment, implementation or a comparable role combining management and execution-heavy tasks. You have managed teams for a meaningful part of that experience

  • You have built an operations function at an early-stage company from the ground up, without a support structure already in place for you to consume

  • You have deployed physical products at customer sites: hardware, robotics, automation or industrial equipment. Robotics or facility services is a strong plus

  • You operate across both horizons at once: what has to happen in the next 12 hours and what the org needs to look like in 3 months. You know at any moment what the top priority is and what to delegate

  • You are hands-on. An undefined process, a missing checklist or one overworked colleague is enough for you to act, fixing it for tomorrow and making sure it does not come back

  • You are the best manager in the room. You set clear goals, put people where their strengths accelerate the team and get along with people from all walks of life.

  • You are detail-oriented and think from first principles, and you can turn that into clear, robust processes that others can just follow

  • You take action on a goal without waiting for direction, and ask for help when you need it without letting that block you

  • Excellent communication in English

What we offer

  • Ownership of Loki’s deployment, internal operations and field ops end-to-end

  • The opportunity to build and lead the operations org as we scale across geographies

  • Close partnership with the founders/leadership team

  • Flat hierarchy, quick decision making and real responsibility in executing Loki’s global expansion

  • Be at the forefront of changing how physical services are delivered

Don’t worry if you don’t hit every checkmark. We value people who learn fast and care about building great products. If Loki excites you and you believe you can help us scale, just give it a go and apply.


At Loki, you are accepted for who you are. We welcome applicants of every background, gender, age and nationality. Different experiences and perspectives make our team and our product better.
