title: Motion Designer
descriptionHtml:
Motion Designer

London / Edinburgh

Wordsmith

Wordsmith is building the legal operations platform for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.

We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents, and disconnected systems.

Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgment matters, and every step is captured as work happens.

We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend, and become a function the business can run with.

More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com, Canva, Starling, and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe, and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

Why this role is different

Motion is one of the fastest ways to show people what Wordsmith actually does.

A strong product animation can communicate more in 30 seconds than a long case study ever will.

This is a founding motion role. You’ll define how Wordsmith moves, feels, and tells product stories through video. You’ll build the systems that let us scale high-quality output and shape how the market experiences our brand.

If you care about craft, speed, and work that directly drives growth, this is a rare opportunity.

The Role

We’re hiring a Motion Designer to own video and motion across Wordsmith.

You’ll create launch videos, feature announcements, social assets, and product storytelling that turns complex workflows into clear, compelling narratives.

You’ll work closely with Design, Growth, Product Marketing, and Founders to bring ideas to life quickly and at a high standard.

This is a hands-on role with real ownership from day one.

What you’ll do

  • Create launch videos, feature announcements, and product animations

  • Turn abstract workflows into clear visual stories that land quickly

  • Build a motion system of templates, transitions, components, and export standards

  • Produce social content, event openers, conference loops, and sales enablement assets

  • Partner with writers, designers, and producers from concept to final delivery

  • Help define how motion supports brand, growth, and product storytelling

  • Use AI tools to improve quality, speed, and creative range

What we’re looking for

  • 3+ years of motion design experience, ideally in-house at a product or technology company

  • Strong reel of shipped work you can talk through clearly

  • Excellent taste and high standards for craft

  • Strong narrative instincts — you can simplify dense ideas visually

  • Ownership mindset — you’re comfortable building a function, not just executing briefs

  • High initiative — you spot gaps and move before being asked

  • AI-first mentality — you actively use modern tools to increase quality and output

  • Advanced skills in After Effects and Figma

  • Comfortable in Premiere for editing

Bonus:

  • Rive, Lottie, GSAP, or web motion

  • 3D tools such as Cinema 4D or Blender

  • AI video tools

  • Experience building reusable motion systems or libraries

How we work

We’re an in-office team. We work together because it helps us move faster, collaborate closely, and produce better work. You should expect to be in the office as your default in your chosen hub.

This is a high trust environment. You’ll have real ownership, clear responsibility, and room to shape how things are done.

We care about pace, but also craft. The standard matters.

This role suits people who want responsibility, autonomy, and visible impact.

What you can expect

  • Ownership of motion at one of Europe’s fastest-growing AI companies

  • Real budget and mandate to build the function properly

  • High-impact work seen by customers, prospects, and the market

  • Close partnership with a senior marketing and design team

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity

Why Wordsmith

We’re growing quickly, shipping fast, and building products customers genuinely need.

There is huge demand, strong momentum, and no shortage of meaningful stories to tell.

If you want your motion work to influence brand, pipeline, and product perception at scale, this is a strong place to do it.

title: Nanofabrication Technician
descriptionHtml:
About Us

QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. We do this with our unique VIO™ technology, the only QPU architecture that breaks the hardware barriers that have held quantum computing back, unlocking the path to MegaQubit quantum processors.

With VIO, we are paving the way for the hyper-scale quantum computers that will change the world. And delivering on that vision demands people who don’t shy away from tackling the hardest challenges of our time. That’s where you come in!

  • Cleanroom Maintenance: Help maintain a pristine working environment, ensuring workstations are prepped, materials are stocked, and cleanroom protocols are strictly followed.

What We Offer:

At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Here’s what you can expect:

Competitive salary - A salary that reflects the impact and importance of the role (and of course 8% holiday allowance)

Pension that’s built to last - A generous and future-proof pension plan that includes partner and dependent coverage.

Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. Work flexibly, in a hybrid setup, with an open vacation policy that lets you manage your time

A connected team - We make space to celebrate wins together, with team events, offsites, and spontaneous moments that bring us closer

Diversity & Inclusion at QuantWare

We’re an ambitious company, not only for our goals but also to become an even more diverse and inclusive team. We know great candidates don't always follow a straight path, and we value diverse experience, perspectives, and ways of thinking. title: Operations Assistant
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for an Operations Assistant to support our Head of Operations with organizing and coordinating the team. You will help keep priorities, meetings, information and follow-ups clear, and help the team stay aligned as our site and production organization grow.

This is a junior, hands-on role for someone who is organized, dependable and eager to learn. You will work closely with the Head of Operations, gain a broad view of how the business runs, and take on more responsibility as you build confidence and experience.

About us

We're a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are building our first production facility and are applying our knowledge toward serial production of solid rocket motors.

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you're excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

Key responsibilities

  • Support the Head of Operations with day-to-day team organization, priorities and follow-through.

  • Coordinate team meetings and check-ins, including calendars, agendas, notes and action tracking.

  • Maintain clear task lists and team schedules, follow up with owners and flag delays or conflicting priorities early.

  • Help the Head of Operations communicate plans, updates and changes clearly to the team.

  • Support onboarding and training coordination for new team members, including practical arrangements and keeping relevant records up to date.

  • Coordinate day-to-day operational needs such as supplies, deliveries, site visits and service appointments with the appropriate team members.

  • Prepare simple status updates, team documents and presentations using information from the relevant owners.

  • Notice recurring coordination problems and help improve team routines, templates and ways of working.

  • Take on small operational tasks and improvement projects, with guidance from the Head of Operations.

What we are looking for

  • 0–3 years of experience in administration, team coordination, operations support, customer service, a working-student role or a similar setting. Relevant internships and practical experience count; extensive experience is not expected.

  • Strong organization and follow-through: you keep track of details, close loops and make sure agreed actions do not get lost.

  • A helpful, reliable and proactive approach. You are comfortable reaching out, asking questions and following up with people respectfully.

  • Clear written and verbal communication and the ability to handle changing priorities calmly.

  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft 365, especially Outlook, Excel, Word and Teams.

  • Discretion when handling confidential business and team information.

descriptionHtml:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

As the first time was a huge success, we're launching version 2 of Partly's Repairer Ambassador Programme — a 3-month, full-time (with flexibility), paid internship for a small cohort of sharp, driven graduates who want real responsibility from day one. This is for people who want something more than a coffee run and a PowerPoint, and will lead to a full-time role for those who make a genuine impact.

Your job is simple: get newly onboarded repair shops actively using the Partly platform as quickly as possible. That means building relationships on the ground, understanding why certain shops aren't placing orders through us, and removing those barriers. You'll become the human face of Partly in repair shops across the UK — someone repairers genuinely trust and enjoy working with.

This is not a desk job. You'll spend your first 1–2 weeks in our London office receiving structured training before heading out to visit customers across your assigned region.

Key details:

  • Contract: 3 months, full-time with flexibility

  • Start: As soon as possible - November 2026

  • Location: UK-wide (field-based, with initial training in London)

💻 What will you do

  • Visit newly signed repair shops across your region and help them get up and running on the Partly platform.

  • Understand why shops aren't placing jobs through Partly and identify practical ways to remove those barriers.

  • Help repairers optimise and streamline their parts procurement workflows.

  • Track repairer activity, monitor adoption, and report insights back to the team on what's working and what isn't.

  • Build authentic, long-term relationships with shop owners and parts managers.

  • Feed customer insights back to the wider business so we can continually improve the product and onboarding experience.

🥷 What we're looking for

  • A recent graduate (university, HND, engineering course, or apprenticeship) with a genuine hunger to learn and get stuck in.

  • Strong common sense and the ability to read a room. This role is all about building trust with people who work with their hands for a living.

  • A full UK driving licence (having your own car is a strong advantage).

title: People Operations Manager
descriptionHtml:
About Conveo

Conveo is the AI research platform enabling fast, affordable, and high quality consumer / B2B research. Global brands like Unilever, Google, and Orange use our AI video interviewer to generate insights across marketing, product, and research teams.


The Context

Conveo is scaling from $4M to $50M, and the People team is running on goodwill and late nights. We have a recruiting team and a new L&D hire joining, but nobody owns the processes and systems underneath them. Compensation schemes, performance cycles and salary reviews all land on Claudia, alongside the daily operational load.

That has to change before we grow further. You'll be the first dedicated People Operations hire, reporting to Claudia. You'll build the operating system for the whole People function: the tools, data, cycles and lifecycle processes that let us hire, pay, develop and support people well across the UK, Belgium and the US.

You'll work closely with Finance on payroll and compensation, with recruiting and L&D on the employee lifecycle, and with managers across the company. When you've done this well, Claudia spends her time on strategy and growing the team, not on firefighting.

Your Mission

1. Own the People systems stack and make it work across every country

You decide how our People tools fit together, then make them run. Today that spans an HRIS, EOR and PEO providers, and payroll across several geographies.

  • Own the HRIS as the single source of truth for every employee, contractor and EOR hire

  • Lead a possible payroll migration end to end: vendor choice, data cleanup, parallel runs, cutover

  • Manage EOR and PEO relationships across the UK, Belgium and the US

  • Connect systems so data flows once, not through spreadsheets and copy-paste

  • Use AI and automation to remove manual admin wherever it adds no judgement

2. Build an employee lifecycle that feels effortless at 2x our size

Every hire, move and exit should follow a clear, repeatable path that works in any country we operate in.

  • Design onboarding, internal moves and offboarding flows with recruiting and L&D

  • Turn tribal knowledge into documented processes and self-serve answers

  • Keep contracts, documents and policies consistent across geographies

  • Make the experience good for employees and managers, not just compliant

3. Run the people cycles the company depends on

Performance reviews, compensation and salary increases should run on time, every time, without pulling Claudia into the detail.

  • Own the performance cycle calendar, tooling and manager enablement

  • Run compensation projects and salary review cycles with Claudia and Finance

  • Keep bands, levels and approvals applied consistently

  • Spot what slowed each cycle down and fix it before the next one

4. Turn People data into decisions

Leadership should be able to answer people questions in minutes, with numbers they trust.

  • Build reliable reporting on headcount, attrition, compensation and cycle completion

  • Keep People data clean enough to support planning and board reporting

  • Give Claudia and managers the insight to act early, not after the fact

What We're Looking For

Must-haves

  • 5+ years in People Operations, including time at a startup or scaleup through hypergrowth, with hands-on experience across multiple countries (ideally Belgium and the UK)

  • Hands-on experience scaling a People function: you've seen what breaks between 50 and 200+ people and helped fix it

  • Strong systems thinking: you design processes and tool stacks that hold up as the company grows, not one-off fixes

  • Hands-on experience implementing an HRIS (Deel is a big plus) and running at least one people cycle (performance, comp review or onboarding) end to end.

  • Comfort working with data: you can build a report leadership trusts, and you notice when the numbers look wrong

Mindset

  • High agency, low ego

  • A builder first: you'd rather design the system than run the same manual process twice

  • Pragmatic about risk: you treat compliance as a baseline, not the whole job

  • Ready to step up and own things you've seen done but haven't led yourself

  • Calm and organised when several cycles land at once

Nice to have

  • Real curiosity about AI, ideally with automations or AI tools you've already put to work in People ops

title: People Operations Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Streaming TV is no longer just a brand awareness channel. It’s becoming a core part of the performance marketing mix, alongside search and social. Vibe.co is building the platform that makes TV work like the rest of the acquisition stack: targeted, measurable, and optimized for results.

Vibe.co is an Audience First Streaming TV Advertising platform that gives marketers the tools to reach the right audiences, optimize campaigns in real time, and understand what’s actually driving business outcomes. With hyper-targeted segmentation, AI-powered recommendations, real-time optimization, and incrementality measurement, Vibe brings the precision and accountability of digital advertising to the biggest screen in the house.

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta.

This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel.

About the Role

You'll join People Ops, the Systems and Operations pillar of the People team. It owns payroll, HRIS, onboarding and offboarding, contracts, benefits, and compliance across France, the US, and our remote geographies. You'll report to Melissa, our Senior Global HR Systems and Operations Manager in Paris. We're opening this role because Vibe is scaling fast across regions, and payroll plus People Ops now need a dedicated owner who keeps the engine running and makes it better. If you want real ownership of payroll from day one, a front-row seat to how an international team actually operates across three geographies, and the room to reshape and automate the work as you go, this is the seat.

What You'll Do

Payroll and contractors

  • Run the monthly French payroll cycle with our external provider, from variable inputs to final validation.

  • Check every payslip before sign-off to catch errors before they reach employees.

  • Keep EOR payroll on schedule across our remote geographies.

  • Own contractor operations end to end, from timesheet collection to the Finance provisioning file.

People operations and HR admin

  • Manage employment documents for a team spread across France, the US, and remote.

  • Administer benefits: enrollments, changes, and the questions employees bring.

  • Run onboarding and offboarding logistics so every joiner and leaver lands cleanly.

Employee support

  • Serve as first point of contact for employees on People questions.

  • Triage incoming requests through our ticketing system against agreed SLAs.

  • Research individual employee cases across policy, contracts, and local labour law.

Systems and projects

  • Maintain HRIS data hygiene and the workflows behind it.

  • Drive People Ops projects end to end, with clear scope, deadlines, and stakeholders.

What You Need

  • 3+ years in payroll, HR administration, or People Ops. An apprenticeship or internship counts.

  • Strong knowledge of French payroll and labour law fundamentals: contracts, absences, final pay, health and provident cover.

  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills and real comfort working with numbers.

  • Project management basics: you've run something with a real deadline and a scope that moved.

  • Experience with an HRIS.

  • Fluent French and English. English is our working language.

Nice to Haves

  • Hands-on experience in a ticketing tool.

  • Exposure to international or EOR payroll.

  • Comfort building automations to cut manual work.

  • Experience at a scale-up.

Our Values

At Vibe, we run on three values: Impact, Ambition, and Urgency. We tie every goal to a real business outcome, think 10x rather than settling for good enough, and move daily rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

You'll thrive here if you own outcomes without needing direction, default to action, and hold yourself to results, not effort.

This is a high-performance environment with high-performance rewards: you'll work alongside people who push you, with real ownership over hard problems in a market that's moving fast.

If that sounds like the best version of your career, we want to meet you.

What We Offer

For candidates in France, the base pay range for this role is €45k–€65k, plus variable. We will support relocation to Paris for great candidates.

Our Interview Process

We respect your time. Here's exactly what to expect, no surprises, no ghosting.

title: Performance Marketing Manager:in (all genders) für Paid Ads, Creatives und KI
descriptionHtml:
Täglich fahren Millionen Autos durch Deutschland, und in den meisten bleibt Platz ungenutzt. Wir ändern das.

MUVN ist ein digitaler Transportmarktplatz. Wir bringen Fahrer:innen mit freiem Laderaum mit Menschen und Unternehmen zusammen, die etwas transportieren müssen. Günstiger, versichert, ohne Umweg.

Unser Wachstum hängt an zwei Seiten gleichzeitig. Wer etwas verschicken will, braucht jemanden, der es mitnimmt. Wer mitnehmen will, braucht Aufträge auf seiner Strecke. Ein Download ist dabei erst der Anfang. Entscheidend ist, ob am Ende ein Transport stattfindet und die Person wiederkommt.

Genau dafür gibt es diese Stelle. Du verantwortest Paid-Kanäle und denkst den ganzen Funnel mit, vom ersten Kontakt mit einer Ad bis zum abgeschlossenen Transport. Zum Start arbeitet dich unser Senior Performance Marketing Manager in alle unsere Tools und Workflows ein, die bei uns KI-first aufgebaut sind.

Du bist nicht die Person, die nur Kosten pro Install drückt. Du willst verstehen, warum Nutzer:innen kommen, wo sie abspringen und welcher Hebel wirklich wirkt. Und du nutzt KI jeden Tag, um schneller zu testen, auszuwerten und zu bauen.

Hierfür suchen wir dich ab dem 01.12. in mit 30h/Woche als Verstärkung für unser Growth-Team in Hamburg 🚀

Aufgaben

  • Paid-Kanäle verantworten

Du steuerst unsere Kampagnen auf Meta, Google, Apple Search Ads und TikTok. Planung, Setup, Budget, tägliche Optimierung. Du entscheidest mit, wo der nächste Euro am meisten bringt.

  • Den ganzen Funnel im Blick

Download, Registrierung, erstes Transportgesuch, Match, abgeschlossener Transport, Wiederkehr. Du optimierst auf die Schritte, die für uns wirklich zählen. Mit Tech sorgst du dafür, dass diese Events sauber gemessen und an die Plattformen zurückgespielt werden.

  • Zwei Seiten, eine Strategie

Wir brauchen Versender:innen und Fahrer:innen, am besten auf denselben Strecken. Du erkennst, wo eine Seite fehlt, und steuerst Kampagnen nach Stadt, Strecke und Kategorie gezielt dagegen.

  • Creative-Pipeline

Du baust eine Pipeline auf, die unsere Ads dauerhaft frisch hält. Briefings, Hooks, UGC, KI-Varianten, Abstimmung mit Design und Content. Du weißt, welches Creative warum funktioniert.

  • Testing-Programm

Du testest systematisch statt nach Bauchgefühl. Von der Hypothese über das Setup bis zur sauberen Auswertung. Learnings dokumentierst du so, dass das ganze Team sie nutzen kann.

  • KI und eigene Tools

Du arbeitest KI-first. Mit Claude Code baust du dir eigene Tools für Auswertung, Reporting, Automatisierung und Creative-Varianten. Was dabei rauskommt, prüfst du. Die Richtigkeit gehört dir, nicht dem Tool.

  • Performance sichtbar machen

Du lieferst ein klares wöchentliches Reporting für Team und Gründer:innen. Nicht nur, was passiert ist, sondern was wir jetzt tun sollten.

  • Trends und Plattform-Änderungen

Neue Formate, Algorithmus-Updates, Veränderungen bei Tracking und Attribution. Du hast sie auf dem Schirm, bevor sie uns treffen, und leitest ab, was das für unsere Kampagnen bedeutet.

  • Datenschnittstelle im Marketing

Du wirst Ansprechperson für Datenfragen aus CRM, SEO und Social Media und verbindest die Zahlen zu einem Bild.

Qualifikation

Du hast mindestens 3 Jahre Erfahrung im Performance Marketing und dabei eigenständig Budget verantwortet. Idealerweise bei einer App, auf einem Marktplatz oder in einem schnell wachsenden Startup.

Meta Ads und Google Ads kennst du in der Tiefe. Du hast Kampagnen nicht nur aufgesetzt, sondern Account-Strukturen gebaut, Budgets über mehrere Kanäle gesteuert und auf Events jenseits des Installs optimiert. Erfahrung mit Apple Search Ads, TikTok, Mobile-Attribution und Tracking-Setups ist ein klares Plus.

Was uns genauso wichtig ist wie Tool-Wissen:

  • Du denkst in Funnels, nicht in Downloads. Ein günstiger Install, aus dem nie ein Transport wird, ist für dich kein Erfolg.

  • Du arbeitest datenbasiert. Du formulierst Hypothesen, testest sauber und sagst auch, wenn ein Test nichts gebracht hat.

  • Du nutzt KI täglich und hast Lust, dir mit Claude Code eigene Workflows zu bauen.

  • Du kennst die Trends im Paid-Bereich und bringst neue Ideen mit, bevor jemand danach fragt.

  • Du triffst Budgetentscheidungen selbst und kannst sie mit Zahlen begründen.

  • Du schreibst Ad Copy, die unsere Zielgruppe wirklich trifft.

Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch. Unser Entwicklungsteam arbeitet auf Englisch.

Driven people > Degrees. Dein Mindset zählt mehr als dein Abschluss.

Benefits

  • Flexible Arbeitsmodelle: Arbeite, wann und wo es für dich am besten passt

  • Hybrides Arbeiten & Remote: Flexibilität ist bei uns Programm

  • Offsites mit dem Team: Gemeinsam erreichen wir mehr

  • Free MUVN Rides: Für dich entstehen keinerlei Nutzungsgebühren

  • Corporate Benefits: Rabatte in hunderten Onlineshops

Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf und deine Antwort auf diese Frage:

Performance Marketing für einen Marktplatz wie MUVN funktioniert anders als für einen Onlineshop oder eine klassische App. Wir brauchen Menschen, die etwas verschicken, und Fahrer:innen, die es mitnehmen, am besten auf derselben Strecke. Was würdest du bei uns anders angehen? Und auf welche Kennzahl würdest du als Erstes schauen?

Es gibt keine richtige Antwort. Uns interessiert, wie du denkst.

Oder schick uns ein kurzes Video dazu. Macht uns ehrlich gesagt noch neugieriger als jedes Anschreiben.

So läuft es ab: erstes Gespräch mit Katharina, dann eine Session mit Jule an einem echten Case aus unseren Kampagnen, dann Kennenlernen mit dem Team.

Fragen? Direkt an Katharina.

Let's get it muvn. 🚀

title: Plateform Security Engineer - CDI Paris - Theodo Cloud
descriptionHtml:
L’histoire du groupe Theodo et son succès Theodo accompagne depuis 2009 les entreprises innovantes dans la conception, le développement et le déploiement de produits digitaux ingénieux - tels que la plateforme TF1+, l'application LCL Pro ou l'application France Identité Numérique - en tirant parti du meilleur de la technologie et de l’approche Lean. Theodo connait une croissance exceptionnelle depuis 15 ans : nos équipes rassemblent plus de 750 Theodoers, principalement des Software Engineers, passionnés de technologie et d’amélioration continue. En 2025, le groupe Theodo génère 100M€ de CA. En 2021, Theodo lance une practice experte en cybersécurité pour aider nos clients à sécuriser leur environnement Cloud. Aujourd'hui, l'équipe compte 11 SecOps Engineers.

Tes missions

Nous intervenons en équipe sur l'essentiel de nos projets : Plateform Security Engineer, SecOps et Project Manager travaillent main dans la main pour garantir l'impact de nos actions chez nos clients.

En tant que Plateform Security Engineer, tu partages ton temps entre trois dimensions:

  • Le delivery technique: tu gardes les mains dans la tech pour contribuer directement à l'avancée des projets : IAM, sécurité réseau, pentest, outils de sécurité Cloud et CI/CD, hardening, secrets management font partie de ton quotidien.

  • La stratégie sécurité: tu es responsable de la stratégie sécurité des projets sur lesquels tu interviens : audits de sécurité, identification de failles, conception d'architectures “secure-by-design”, remédiations pragmatiques, mise en conformité.

  • La montée en compétence de l'équipe: tu contribues à la progression des SecOps avec qui tu travailles, via de la formation, du pair programming et du coaching.

Tu auras également l'opportunité de t'impliquer sur des projets internes à Theodo Cloud : l'amélioration de nos standards de sécurité, la construction de formations, la veille technique et le thought leadership (articles, talks).

Les opportunités d'évolution

Nous proposons une évolution possible à nos Plateform Security Engineers vers un rôle d'Engineering Manager, que ce soit sur un axe management et/ou un axe expertise technique.

Profil recherché

Nous recherchons une personne ayant :

  • 3 à 5 ans d'expérience minimum sur un poste de Plateform Security Engineer ou DevSecOps

  • L'habitude de travailler sur une stack technique moderne : Kubernetes, Terraform, cloud providers publics (AWS, GCP, Azure)…

  • Une maîtrise des concepts de sécurité infrastructure : IAM avancé, sécurité réseau (VPC, firewalls, WAF), CI/CD, méthodologies de pentest et d'audit

  • Le goût du partage de compétences : tu as déjà accompagné la montée en compétence d'un ou plusieurs collègues (pair programming, mentoring, formation) et ça te donne envie d'en faire plus

  • L'envie de contribuer à la croissance d'une practice encore jeune, en participant à la structuration de nos méthodes, de nos formations ou de notre présence externe (articles, talks)

Tu ne coches pas 100% des critères mais tu penses tout de même correspondre à notre recherche ? Ne t'auto-censure pas et envoie-nous ta candidature, on se fera un plaisir de l'étudier !

Pour information

  • Le poste est proposé en CDI, basé depuis nos locaux à Paris.

  • Nous permettons à nos équipes de télé-travailler jusqu'à 2 jours par semaine.

  • Le salaire proposé dépend du niveau d’expérience de chacun : nous en parlons toujours dès le premier appel téléphonique.

Déroulement des entretiens

Nous répondons à toutes les candidatures dans un délai de 3 jours.

Si ton profil nous intéresse, nous te proposons le process suivant :

  1. Un appel téléphonique de 30 minutes avec un membre de l'équipe recrutement, pour comprendre tes critères de recherche.

  2. Un entretien d'une heure avec le recruteur ou la recruteuse avec qui tu as échangé à la première étape, pour parler plus en détail de la culture Theodo Cloud.

  3. Un entretien technique d'1h de mise en situation autour d’un schéma d’architecture

  4. Un entretien technique d’1h autour d’un exercice sur une VM

  5. Un échange avec notre Partner cybersécurité.

Notre process dure en moyenne 2 semaines.

Tu seras accompagné(e) par une personne de l'équipe recrutement, qui sera là pour te coacher tout au long du process.

descriptionHtml:

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full.

 


How you'll make impact

You’ll help businesses bring financial services directly into their own products, using Airwallex’s embedded finance infrastructure to support their customers across markets. You’ll own complex, consultative sales cycles from prospecting and discovery through commercial negotiation, contract signature and launch.

  • Build relationships with vertical SaaS companies, marketplaces, fintechs and other platforms.

  • Help customers embed accounts, payments, payouts, FX and cards into their products.

You’ll work from our London office three days a week.

Essentials

Equal opportunity

Airwallex is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and anyone seeking employment at Airwallex is considered based on merit, qualifications, competence and talent. We don’t regard color, religion, race, national origin, sexual orientation, ancestry, citizenship, sex, marital or family status, disability, gender, or any other legally protected status when making our hiring decisions. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

title: Platform Reliability Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.  

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability. 

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally. 

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers. 

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale. 

AI FactoryOS Operations 

AI FactoryOS is Firmus' proprietary operating system for the AI Factory. It governs GPU telemetry, cooling, power and grid interaction as one integrated layer, so that every Firmus site can be optimised and monitored as a single system. 

AI FactoryOS Operations runs that platform in production and owns the 24/7 reliability of AI FactoryOS, Firmus AI Cloud and the platforms built on them, together with the service levels the estate is measured against. 

The remit is an engineering one. The function builds the guarded automation, remediation and operational tooling that turn manual response into a software-defined capability, and builds and operates the shared services the estate's own operation depends on. The function works closely with the engineering teams that build the platform, supplying the production evidence that shapes what they fix and what they build next. 

Role Summary  

Firmus runs large-scale, state-of-the-art AI infrastructure built on the latest generation of GPU rack-scale systems and operated as one estate to power the next generation of AI innovation. The Platform Reliability Engineer is part of the team that operates the platform services Firmus AI Cloud runs on in production: the GPU compute fleet, exabyte-scale storage, the multi-tenant control and management plane, and the virtualisation and shared services that host it. Together, these are the foundation every customer workload depends on.

This is a hands-on site reliability engineering role that works across the stack, from Linux and Kubernetes to storage, virtualisation and the compute fleet. The team runs each service to a declared service level, measures reliability against it, and treats operations as a software problem, engineering repetitive manual work out of the system rather than absorbing it. The role picks up incidents escalated from first response, owns each one through to resolution, and works across teams and vendors to restore service, bringing in specialist engineers when a fault needs deeper investigation. Automation is a first-class part of the role: faults are diagnosed using the observability stack, post-incident reviews feed fixes back into the platform, and every resolved fault is a candidate for a runbook or an automated fix.

Key Responsibilities

  • Triage, diagnose and resolve incidents across the stack, including Kubernetes clusters and workloads, storage, virtualisation, network connectivity and the underlying Linux hosts, owning each incident from escalation through to resolution.
  • Operate the multi-tenant control and management plane that Firmus' AI and infrastructure services depend on, including the tenancy, quota and access controls that support separation between tenant workloads and data.
  • Operate the virtualisation platform that hosts the management plane, and the shared services that run on it, to their declared service levels.
  • Operate Firmus' exabyte-scale distributed and high-performance filesystems and S3-compatible object storage to their declared service levels, handling capacity, performance and availability incidents and escalating to specialist engineers and vendors (for example VAST or WEKA) with clear evidence when further investigation is needed.
  • Operate the GPU compute fleet in production: node health and readiness, GPU and node fault detection and handling, firmware and driver currency to the supported baselines, remediation and return to service, and support for cluster provisioning and validation activities.
  • Reduce toil by converting repeat fixes into runbooks and automated remediation delivered as controlled code, contributing to the team's automation and remediation tooling.
  • Diagnose performance problems across the data path between compute and storage, gathering the evidence needed to resolve them and working with network and storage specialists where required.
  • Deliver change as code through the agreed change process, with peer review, testing, staged rollout where applicable, and a rollback plan.
  • Use the observability stack (for example Grafana, Prometheus, Loki and Tempo) to track service level indicators against their objectives, query metrics, logs and traces, correlate signals across services and diagnose faults, and improve dashboards and alerting so that each alert is actionable and tied to a runbook.
  • Execute the patching cycle and urgent vulnerability remediation across the services the team operates.
  • Manage vendor support cases across the hardware and software portfolio, raising and tracking cases under the relevant support agreements, supplying logs and diagnostic evidence, and following cases through to agreed response and resolution times.
  • Take part in technical recovery during major incidents and in blameless post-incident reviews, feed recurring issues back to the engineering teams as clear requirements, share the follow-the-sun on-call roster, and keep incident tickets, operational procedures and runbooks accurate and current so that others can execute them successfully.

Skills & Experience 

Required Skills

  • Solid experience operating production infrastructure in a 24/7 environment using site reliability engineering practices, including service level objectives, toil reduction, owning incidents from escalation to resolution, oncall participation, post-incident review and writing runbooks that others can execute successfully.
  • Strong working knowledge of Linux systems administration and troubleshooting, including storage, host networking, processes, memory and I/O, and a systematic approach to isolating faults.
  • Working experience with scale-out, parallel or enterprise storage (for example VAST, WEKA, Ceph, Lustre, GPFS or NetApp), including diagnosing performance and capacity problems using evidence rather than assumption.
  • Familiarity with a virtualisation platform (for example Proxmox, VMware or KVM).
  • Working experience using observability tooling to diagnose faults (for example Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo or Elasticsearch), including writing queries across metrics and logs (such as PromQL and LogQL) and correlating signals across services.
  • Working experience with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps practices (for example OpenTofu or Terraform, Ansible, Argo CD), and writing scripts or small tools for operational automation in a language such as Python or Go.
  • Familiarity with server hardware operation and support, including working with hardware and software vendors to raise support cases and supply diagnostic evidence.Platform Reliability Engineer
  • Familiarity with cyber security principles and how they apply to operating production infrastructure.
  • Clear communication skills, with the ability to write incident updates, ticket notes and escalations that others can act on, and a working style suited to a team that shares accountability for a broad portfolio across regions.


Preferred Experience

  • Experience in infrastructure operations for GPU or HPC environments and the demands of large-scale distributed training and inference, including GPU health and fault signals (for example DCGM health checks, NCCL tests and XID errors).
  • Experience in multi-tenant service provider, cloud or colocation environments with contractual response commitments and customer-facing reporting.
  • Working knowledge of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, routing, VLANs, load balancing and firewalls, and the ability to trace a connectivity fault across hosts, switches and services.
  • Knowledge of high-performance fabrics and data-path technologies, such as InfiniBand, RoCE, RDMA and GPUDirect Storage, and DPU or SmartNIC-based networking.
  • Familiarity with bare-metal lifecycle and provisioning automation (for example NVIDIA Infra Controller, MAAS, Ironic or Metal3), and standard operating environments with known good-state enforcement.
  • Hands-on experience operating and troubleshooting Kubernetes, including workloads, networking, storage and cluster health, and multi-tenant and GPU-enabled Kubernetes patterns.
  • Experience with ITSM and incident management tooling (for example Jira Service Management, ServiceNow or PagerDuty).
  • Experience working under ISO 27001 or SOC 2 controls.
  • Relevant certification, such as Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), a Linux certification (for example RHCSA or LFCS), or a vendor certification.
  • A Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and training.

Location & Reporting 

Location: Based in Australia or Singapore, with travel to Australian AI Factory sites as required. 

On-call: The function runs 24/7. First line monitoring and first response sit with the operations centre. This role shares the after-hours escalation roster for its domain with the other senior engineers in the function. 

Reporting to:  Reports to the Head of AI FactoryOS Operations while the function is being established, working under broad direction with a high degree of autonomy and direct access to the decision makers. As the function reaches its planned structure, the role will report to the Infrastructure Operations Manager, with the Head of AI FactoryOS Operations remaining accountable for the function. The scope, level and remit of the role do not change under either arrangement. 

Employment Basis

Permanent full-time

Diversity

At Firmus, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds who are passionate about creating a more sustainable future through innovative engineering solutions.

Join us in our mission to revolutionize the AI industry through sustainable practices and cutting-edge engineering. Apply now to be part of shaping the future of sustainable AI infrastructure.

title: Principal Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Principal Engineer - Contract

About this role

The bar has moved. Five years ago a strong engineer was measured by what they could build and how well they could mentor others to build it. Today, with Claude Code and agents, we produce quality work at a speed that would have looked superhuman in 2022 (Podium, PayPoint, Zuto, RL, OAG Analyser and others).

What separates exceptional from good is no longer typing speed or local craftsmanship. It is the complete package: architecture, deep engineering foundations, communication, system thinking, and the judgement to direct both your own intelligence and AI toward outcomes that matter.

Exceptional people at this level are not the best implementer in the room; they are the person whose specifications, decisions, and review judgement compound into systems that work in production and that others (and agents) can build on. They are a force multiplier, they hold a room at the highest levels, and clients treat them as the SME by default.

Your mindset

The mindset is the engine, and it is almost impossible to teach retrospectively. You are outcome obsessed, not output obsessed and you care whether the problem was actually solved - you resist the ego instinct to admire a clever solution and ask whether it was needed at all.

You are intellectually honest about uncertainty, taking a trust-but-verify approach and assuming the surprising bug is the one that will burn. You are deeply pragmatic, which matters at CreateFuture where pace counts: you have outgrown the religious wars about platforms, languages and patterns, you hold opinions loosely, and you decide for the systems in front of you, not the ones you wish you had.

You have a bias toward delivery: the smallest thing that works, then iterate, treating documents and meetings as means to that end.

And you are relentlessly curious beyond any immediate need, wanting to know how the database actually stores things or why a Claude Opus inference call costs what it does, which keeps you several layers ahead while the rest of the team is still reading the API docs.

AI as the accelerant

For a Principal to be truly exceptional, this is now already a first-class competency in your arsenal, not a side skill. An engineer who is brilliant by last year's standards but not fluent with AI is not exceptional in 2026. In practice that means:

  • Setting AI up to succeed. You treat context engineering as a craft (the right files, specs, examples and constraints), and you architect systems with clean interfaces, good naming, machine-readable specs and knowledge bases so the codebase is a quality baseline AI can work on later. No separate ivory-tower architect required.
    Reviewing and choosing well. You read far more code than you write, and your value is in the quality of review: catching the silent assumption, the security flaw, the architectural drift, knowing where models fail and looking there first. You pick the right tool for the job (Claude Code for a deep refactor, an inline assistant when that is enough, a sub-agent for parallel work, the right model for analysis versus generation) and you know the constraints differ by client, an enterprise like PayPoint or Natwest versus a scale-up type business like Zuto or OAG.
    Working with non-determinism. You see where AI moves the bottleneck and help people left and right of you unblock the value stream. You build with AI components but know success is no longer a binary, reaching for evals, golden datasets, structured outputs and fallback paths as naturally as you reach for unit tests.

Technical breadth across the full stack

Exceptional means depth in at least one area but competence everywhere the system reaches.

  • Backend: an instinct for distributed systems (what fails, what is eventually consistent, where queues back up), APIs that age well, thoughtful data modelling, and an understanding that languages are mostly syntax differences you can close with AI.
    Cloud: cost-aware and security-aware by default, reaching for IaC, composing the primitives rather than stitching together managed services and hoping it works.
    Data: modern pipelines, governance and lineage, increasingly vector stores and embeddings, with data quality treated as seriously as production code because garbage in, garbage out is far worse once AI features depend on it.
    Web and mobile: past the framework arguments, with a clear view on what you would pick today, and able to build "good enough" front ends yourself with AI.

Full-stack here means seeing the platform as one system and knowing which levers matter most. It does not mean front-end work with a few Node.js servers.

System thinking, consulting and commercial judgement

At CreateFuture we work in a consultancy context, where many otherwise excellent IC engineers can struggle.

You know technology is roughly 30% of the picture; the rest is design, argument and reasoning, commercial and political acumen, and the clarity to frame outcomes for a COO, CTO, CIO or CEO in their own language.

You know when gold-plating is wasteful, you can name when a project's real problem is not technical and say so even when it is awkward, and you have a strong sense of what is durable versus what is fashion.

You are not the engineer who introduced the team to seven new technologies last year; you are the one who removed three and quietly made the remaining stack stronger.

Leadership mentality

Technical work is necessary but no longer sufficient. By default you raise the level of everyone around you, regardless of discipline.

  • Communicate clearly and frequently (documents, decisions, post-mortems, design notes); the written artefact is the machine-readable context we can feed to AI later.
  • Make decisions and own them. You don't escalate everything or hoard control, and you are willing to be the benevolent dictator when it is your turn.
  • Mentor in AI fluency, not just code: tooling, prompting and review discipline, so your team is twice as productive a year from now.
  • Need little line management. You communicate upwards, raise by exception, self-resolve, and can be trusted with financial controls.
  • Disagree well. You tell people they are wrong with evidence and no ego, and you change your own mind when you are shown to be wrong.

What we're not looking for

  • The gifted engineer who sits in a silo. This is a team game.
  • The one who is fluent with AI but ships without the guardrails and quality gates enterprise clients expect.
  • The one with strong technical opinions who cannot justify them commercially and gets defensive when challenged.
  • The pure manager who wants to orchestrate teams rather than get involved. This is about setting a new standard, not coordinating it.
  • The engineer who will not immerse in a client environment. This role will mean on-site work and trusted relationships built in person. We are not going back to working away from the client and being bypassed.

What we’ll offer you:

We trust people to do their best work. That means flexibility over rigid rules, impact over activity, and real investment in your growth both professionally and personally. You’ll be part of a supportive, and friendly culture, surrounded by smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do.

We offer flexible working, including hybrid and remote options. Our office hubs are located in Edinburgh, Leeds, Manchester, London and Bulgaria, with occasional travel to client sites or CreateFuture offices when needed.

We trust you to manage your time balancing collaboration with client time and focused work. What matters is the impact you have, not how busy you look.

We try to keep our hiring process clear, fair and respectful of your time. We aim to get back to everyone who applies and we will be upfront about where you are in the process.

descriptionHtml:
About SchemeServe

SchemeServe is insurance software like no other.

Hosted in the cloud for MGAs, brokers and insurers, the SchemeServe platform boasts unique flexibility, unstoppable innovation and truly Obsessive Support.

Started in 2000 by our CEO, Adam, SchemeServe has grown from strength to strength, never having taken outside investment. We're proud of how far we've come and how loyal we've stayed to our Core Values.

We're fully remote (we were doing it before it was fashionable!), although we get together twice a year for Team Retreats.

We prize self-development and encourage everyone to keep learning and challenging themselves. Free books? Mentoring? Professional development? You got it.

We also offer flexible working, paid charity days, a fantastic, relaxed and open company culture and free biscuits through the post.

We genuinely believe this is the best place you could ever work.

If you're excited, good! So are we.

Come and join the Insurtech revolution!

Principal Backend Engineer

UK Remote

We're looking for an exceptional Principal Backend Engineer to help make backend engineering across SchemeServe better.

You'll be one of the most technically experienced engineers in the organisation and the CTO's primary technical partner for backend engineering, helping shape our architecture, engineering principles and technical direction.

But this isn't primarily a feature delivery role and your job isn't to personally build everything you help design.

Your real job is to make our engineering organisation better at building great software.

You'll work alongside engineers and teams, helping solve difficult problems, challenging their thinking and developing their technical skills and judgement.

What We Mean By Principal



This is a deeply technical role.

You'll need the depth to understand complex backend systems, architecture, security, performance, resilience and maintainability; review designs and implementations; spot risks; and challenge experienced engineers.

But technical knowledge alone isn't enough.

We want someone who understands there isn't always one "correct" way to build software.

Patterns, standards and best practices are useful tools. They aren't commandments.

We care about finding the most appropriate solution to the problem in front of us.

That means understanding the problem, business, existing platform, risks and likely future – and making pragmatic decisions based on the trade-offs.

Sometimes the right answer will be a new service or technology.

Sometimes it'll be improving what we already have.

Sometimes the boring solution really is the best solution.

We're quite comfortable with that.

How You'll Lead



Success in this role comes through influence rather than authority.

We don't want every difficult technical decision to end with:

"We'd better ask the Principal Engineer."

If an engineer proposes an approach you disagree with, we don't just want you to replace it with your own.

Understand their thinking. Ask questions. Challenge assumptions. Explore the trade-offs. Share your experience.

And be prepared to change your own mind too.

The goal is to leave that engineer better equipped to solve the next problem, not just holding the answer to this one.

Your technical impact should multiply through the people around you.

You'll remain close enough to the code to understand what's actually happening and occasionally roll up your sleeves to prototype, investigate a difficult problem or unblock a team.

But if after a year you've personally written loads of brilliant software while everyone around you is working exactly as they were before, we haven't succeeded.

The Technical Challenge



Our platform has been evolving for more than 25 years.

At its heart is a mature C# .NET Framework 4.7 monolith, alongside an expanding ecosystem of modern C# .NET 10 and TypeScript services.

Our backend estate includes:


  • .NET Framework and modern C#/.NET.
  • TypeScript services.
  • Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL and Redis.
  • Azure cloud infrastructure.
  • Cloudflare platform services.
  • API-first architecture.
  • Git-based development workflows.


We're continuing to modernise, but we're not interested in modernisation for modernisation's sake.

We aren't trying to win an award for having the most fashionable architecture diagram.

We want a secure, reliable and maintainable platform that can support SchemeServe for many years to come – and we want you to help us decide what should evolve and, just as importantly, what doesn't need changing.

What You'll Do



You'll work closely with our CTO and engineering teams to:


  • Shape our backend engineering strategy, architecture and technical direction.
  • Help engineers make better technical and architectural decisions.
  • Develop sensible engineering principles and guardrails without replacing good judgement with rules.
  • Guide the continued evolution of our monolith and modern service-based platform.
  • Coach and mentor engineers, developing their technical skills and judgement.
  • Review significant designs and architectural decisions and challenge unnecessary complexity.
  • Champion security, quality, testing, observability, resilience and performance.
  • Identify technical risks and help teams navigate them.
  • Evaluate technologies and patterns based on their value to SchemeServe rather than their popularity elsewhere.
  • Balance long-term engineering quality with short-term business needs.
  • Occasionally contribute directly to implementation when that's genuinely the best way to help.
  • Be a generally awesome person.


What We're Looking For



You'll need:


  • Deep expertise in modern backend engineering and strong commercial C#/.NET experience.
  • Strong knowledge of software architecture, distributed systems and API design.
  • Experience with mature legacy applications and modern service-oriented architectures.
  • Strong cloud architecture experience, ideally Azure.
  • Excellent understanding of databases, security, testing, maintainability and modern software delivery.
  • Experience shaping engineering principles and practices across teams.
  • A track record of making engineers around you better through mentoring, coaching and technical leadership.
  • The ability to challenge experienced engineers constructively without becoming a gatekeeper.
  • Strong opinions, loosely held – the confidence to challenge and the humility to change your mind.
  • Excellent communication and the ability to influence without relying on authority.
  • Excellent technical judgement, balancing quality, complexity, risk, cost and business value.


Most importantly, we're looking for someone who asks:

"What's the right solution for us?"

rather than:

"What's the way everyone else is doing it?"

Nice To Have


  • Experience modernising large monolithic applications.
  • Commercial TypeScript backend experience.
  • Cloudflare or edge technology experience.
  • SaaS platforms at scale.
  • Financial services, insurance or another regulated industry.
  • Observability, platform engineering or SRE experience.
  • AI-assisted development and engineering productivity tooling.


You don't need to tick every box.

If you've got the technical depth, judgement and ability to make engineers around you better, we'd rather have a conversation than lose a great candidate because you haven't used one particular technology.

What Success Looks Like



Within your first year:


  • Engineers are making stronger technical and architectural decisions with greater confidence.
  • Our engineering principles are understood rather than blindly followed.
  • Technical discussions are constructive, pragmatic and result in clear decisions.
  • Security, reliability, maintainability and performance concerns are identified earlier.
  • We've made sensible progress modernising our platform without adding complexity for complexity's sake.
  • You've made a lasting positive impact on both our software and the people who build it.


Ultimately, we don't want SchemeServe to become dependent on you for every difficult technical decision.

We want SchemeServe to become better at making those decisions because you're here.

title: Product Certification Engineer, Fuel Cell Systems
descriptionHtml:
About EH Energy Engineering

EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland. We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements, so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate.

 

Key responsibilities

Certification strategy and project management

  • Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

  • Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

  • Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

Safety engineering and risk analysis

  • Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

  • Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

  • Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

  • Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

Compliance and technical documentation

  • Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

  • Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

  • Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

  • Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

Collaboration and continuous improvement

  • Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

  • Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

Standards and regulatory scope

The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

  • IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

     

Required qualifications

  • Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

  • 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

  • Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

  • Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

  • Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

  • Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

  • Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

  • Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

  • Fluent English, written and spoken

     

Preferred qualifications and personal profile

Nice to have

  • Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

  • Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

  • Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

  • Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

Personal profile

  • Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

  • Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

  • Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

  • Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

     

Start date: Immediately

descriptionHtml:
Zone & Company Software Consulting LLC (“Zone”) is the ERP-native AI platform for financial operations, purpose-built for organizations running on Oracle NetSuite. We are redefining how finance teams operate by delivering an AI-powered system that automates, connects, and scales financial workflows directly within the ERP.

As the AI operating system for finance teams in NetSuite, Zone enables more than 4,500 customers worldwide to run smarter, faster, and with greater accuracy. Our platform spans the full financial lifecycle, including Quote-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Treasury, Payroll Management, and Record-to-Report, eliminating manual processes and unlocking real-time financial intelligence.

By embedding intelligence directly into NetSuite, Zone helps finance teams move beyond reactive work to proactive, strategic impact. Learn more at www.zoneandco.com or follow us on LinkedIn: linkedin.com/company/zoneandco.

About the Job

The Product Manager owns strategy, roadmap, and execution for the Procure-to-Pay (P2P) domain of the Zone & Co platform — covering procurement, vendor management, AP automation, invoice capture, approvals, and payments. Reporting to the Director of Product, this role spans the full product lifecycle, from discovery through launch and ongoing health of live features.

You'll translate complex AP/procurement workflows (requisition-to-approval, three-way match, invoice capture, payment execution) into intuitive software built natively on Oracle NetSuite. This is a ground-floor opportunity in "Agentic Finance" — you'll spend more time in working prototypes than slide decks, using AI to move from insight to demo in hours, and you'll define how autonomous agents earn user trust in a domain where accuracy is non-negotiable.

  • Partner with Sales and Marketing on GTM strategy and enablement

What You'll Need

Required

  • Strong Agile/Scrum skills and familiarity with tools like Jira or Productboard
  • Proven success in fully remote, async, globally distributed teams
  • Excellent communicator, able to translate compliance logic into simple software

Preferred

  • Experience with Oracle NetSuite or a comparable native ERP platform
  • Familiarity with P2P/spend tools (Coupa, Ariba, Bill.com, Tipalti, AvidXchange, Ramp) and OCR/document capture

  • Experience scaling products in high-growth (Series C–D) environments

Benefits

At Zone, we provide the platform; you provide the grit. We operate as a high-velocity, fully remote, global team where autonomy isn't just a perk, it’s the standard. We’re looking for self-driven professionals eager to navigate the complexities of a unique SaaS environment and take full command of their professional evolution.

We ditch micro-management for high-trust flexibility, ensuring you have the space to innovate and scale. Our benefits are built to fuel this lifestyle, supporting your life beyond the screen so you can focus on making a global impact. Explore our offerings at https://www.zoneandco.com/careers

Join Our Global Mission

title: Product Marketer
descriptionHtml:
About Dust

Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it.

With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done.

With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

Summary

Dust is looking for a Product Marketer to shape how we bring a fast-moving, technical product to market and build the engine behind our product launches.

You will lead product launches and storytelling at Dust, turning a constant stream of product innovation into clear positioning, compelling narratives, and launches that help customers understand what’s new, why it matters, and what they can do with it.

This is a hands-on role. You will work closely with product and engineering to understand what we’re building, find the story within it, and bring that story to life across messaging, web, video, social, customer communications, and sales enablement. You’ll own the work from strategy through execution, bringing in designers, contractors, and other partners where they can add specialist expertise.

It’s a rare opportunity to help define the product narrative of a category-defining AI company while the product, the market, and the way people work with AI are all evolving quickly.

What you'll do

Own Dust’s product launch motion

  • Own product launches from initial narrative and positioning through asset creation, amplification strategy, and sales enablement

  • Build and run an always-on launch program that keeps pace with Dust’s rapid product development, supporting at least 5-7 releases each quarter

  • Partner closely with engineering team to understand what’s shipping, why it matters, and which initiatives require a broader market moment

  • Establish lightweight launch tiers and processes that bring consistency without slowing the team down

Turn product innovation into compelling stories

  • Develop positioning and messaging for new capabilities, translating technical innovation into clear, differentiated narratives that resonate with Dust’s buyers and users

  • Create launch assets across formats, including short-form videos, social campaigns, web copy, blogs, livestream events, customer communications, and sales collateral

  • Develop unique, scroll-stopping feature overview videos by owning storyboarding and screen capture end-to-end, while leveraging in-house creative and design support or external contractors as needed

  • Experiment with new formats and approaches to find the most effective ways to make Dust’s product understandable, memorable, and exciting

Become a trusted partner to product and engineering

  • Build strong relationships with engineers and user leads and become a partner they proactively bring into product launches

  • Develop enough technical fluency to ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and uncover the most important customer and market story

  • Operate effectively in Dust’s highly autonomous product environment, where engineers often lead product initiatives directly

  • Bring customer, competitive, and market context into conversations about how we position and communicate the product

  • Partner with Dust’s founders and marketing leadership on major product narratives and moments

Connect product storytelling across the business

  • Equip Sales and Customer Success teams with the messaging, assets, and context they need to effectively pitch new capabilities to customers

  • Partner with Brand & Content to turn product innovation into broader editorial and content opportunities

  • Work with Growth and Field Marketing to extend launches across campaigns, events, and distribution channels

  • Ensure Dust’s product positioning and differentiation remain clear and consistent as the platform evolves

  • Create a reliable pipeline of high-quality product content that teams across Dust can use and distribute

What you’ll bring

  • 3–5+ years of dedicated product marketing experience, ideally with strong PMM foundations from an established B2B technology company and hands-on experience in a high-growth startup

  • A track record of personally owning technical B2B product or feature launches from positioning through execution

  • Exceptional product storytelling skills, with the ability to make complex technology clear, credible, and compelling

  • The range to create across formats, including positioning and messaging, web, written content, social, presentations, and video or demo storytelling

  • Strong technical curiosity and the ability to build credibility with engineers by asking thoughtful questions and quickly getting fluent in the product

  • Strong taste and an informed point of view on what great modern product marketing looks like

  • Comfort operating with ambiguity and figuring out the right approach rather than defaulting to an established playbook

  • A hands-on working style. You’re as comfortable writing the copy, developing the storyboard, or building the launch plan as you are setting the strategy

  • Deep fluency in and curiosity about AI. You’ll use Dust to run your own function and become deeply familiar with how our customers are putting AI to work

  • Based in Paris

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

  • Our product constitution, a story about our mission

  • Your Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. A conversation about AI agents taking on larger parts of work and how teams collaborate with them.

  • Dust: Gabriel Hubert on Enterprise AI, Gabriel Hubert, Nasdaq, published May 7, 2026. On Dust’s approach to enterprise AI and building the company in Europe.
